5.44.s:
munaya ūcuḥ |
vyāsotpattiṃ mahābuddhe brūhi sūta dayānidhe |
kṛpayā parayā svāmin kṛtārthānnaḥ kuru prabho ||
5.44.d:
मुनय ऊचुः ।
व्यासोत्पत्तिं महाबुद्धे ब्रूहि सूत दयानिधे ।
कृपया परया स्वामिन् कृतार्थान्नः कुरु प्रभो ॥
5.44.m: The sages said: / Speak of the birth of Vyāsa, O great intellect, Sūta, treasure-house of compassion; / out of supreme mercy, O master, fulfill our purpose, O lord.

5.44.s:
vyāsasya jananī proktā nāmnā satyavatī śubhā |
vivāhitā tu sā devī rājñā śantanunā kila ||
5.44.d:
व्यासस्य जननी प्रोक्ता नाम्ना सत्यवती शुभा ।
विवाहिता तु सा देवी राज्ञा शन्तनुना किल ॥
5.44.m: The auspicious mother of Vyāsa is said to have been named Satyavatī; / indeed, that lady was married by King Śantanu.

5.44.s:
tasyāṃ jāto mahāyogī kathaṃ vyāsaḥ parāśarāt |
sandeho'tra mahāñjātastaṃ bhavāñchettumarhati ||
5.44.d:
तस्यां जातो महायोगी कथं व्यासः पराशरात् ।
सन्देहोऽत्र महाञ्जातस्तं भवाञ्छेत्तुमर्हति ॥
5.44.m: How was the great yogin Vyāsa born from her through Parāśara? / A great doubt has arisen here; you ought to resolve it.

5.44.s:
sūta uvāca |
ekadā tīrthayātrāyāṃ vrajanyogī parāśaraḥ |
yadṛcchayāgato ramyaṃ yamunāyāstaṭaṃ śubham ||
5.44.d:
सूत उवाच ।
एकदा तीर्थयात्रायां व्रजन्योगी पराशरः ।
यदृच्छयागतो रम्यं यमुनायास्तटं शुभम् ॥
5.44.m: Sūta said: / Once, while wandering on a pilgrimage, the yogin Parāśara / came by chance to the charming, auspicious bank of the Yamunā.

5.44.s:
niṣādamāha dharmātmā kurvantaṃ bhojanaṃ tadā |
nayasva yamunāpāraṃ jalayānena māmaram ||
5.44.d:
निषादमाह धर्मात्मा कुर्वन्तं भोजनं तदा ।
नयस्व यमुनापारं जलयानेन मामरम् ॥
5.44.m: The righteous sage then spoke to a Niṣāda who was taking his meal: / 'Take me across the Yamunā swiftly in a boat.'

5.44.s:
ityukto muninā tena niṣādaḥ svasutāṃ jagau |
matsyagandhāmamuṃ bāle pāraṃ nāvā naya drutam ||
5.44.d:
इत्युक्तो मुनिना तेन निषादः स्वसुतां जगौ ।
मत्स्यगन्धाममुं बाले पारं नावा नय द्रुतम् ॥
5.44.m: Spoken to thus by that sage, the Niṣāda said to his daughter, / Matsyagandhā: 'O child, take him quickly across in the boat.

5.44.s:
tāpaso'yaṃ mahābhāge dṛśyantīgarbhasambhavaḥ |
titīrṣurasti dharmābdhiścaturāmnāyapāragaḥ ||
5.44.d:
तापसोऽयं महाभागे दृश्यन्तीगर्भसम्भवः ।
तितीर्षुरस्ति धर्माब्धिश्चतुराम्नायपारगः ॥
5.44.m: This ascetic, O fortunate girl, born from the womb of Dṛśyantī, / desires to cross over; he is an ocean of righteousness, one who has crossed to the far shore of the four Vedas.'

5.44.s:
iti vijñāpitā pitrā matsyagandhā mahāmunim |
saṃvāhayati naukāyāmāsīnaṃ sūryarociṣam ||
5.44.d:
इति विज्ञापिता पित्रा मत्स्यगन्धा महामुनिम् ।
संवाहयति नौकायामासीनं सूर्यरोचिषम् ॥
5.44.m: Instructed thus by her father, Matsyagandhā ferried / the great sage, who shone with the brilliance of the sun and sat in the boat.

5.44.s:
kālayogānmahāyogī tasyāṃ kāmāturo'bhavat |
dṛṣṭvā yo'psarasāṃ rūpaṃ na kadāpi vimohitaḥ ||
5.44.d:
कालयोगान्महायोगी तस्यां कामातुरोऽभवत् ।
दृष्ट्वा योऽप्सरसां रूपं न कदापि विमोहितः ॥
5.44.m: Through the course of time, the great yogin became afflicted with desire for her— / he who, upon seeing the beauty of apsarases, was never bewildered at any time.

5.44.s:
grahītukāmaḥ sa munirdāśakanyāṃ manoharām |
dakṣiṇena kareṇaitāmaspṛśaddakṣiṇe kare ||
5.44.d:
ग्रहीतुकामः स मुनिर्दाशकन्यां मनोहराम् ।
दक्षिणेन करेणैतामस्पृशद्दक्षिणे करे ॥
5.44.m: Desiring to grasp that lovely fisherman’s daughter, the sage / touched her right hand with his right hand.

5.44.s:
tamuvāca viśālākṣī vacanaṃ smitapūrvakam |
kimidaṃ kriyate karma vācaṃyamavigarhitam ||
5.44.d:
तमुवाच विशालाक्षी वचनं स्मितपूर्वकम् ।
किमिदं क्रियते कर्म वाचंयमविगर्हितम् ॥
5.44.m: The large-eyed girl said to him with a smile: / “What is this action being done, which is condemned by the restrained of speech?

5.44.s:
vasiṣṭhasya kule ramye tvaṃ jāto'si mahāmate |
niṣādajā tvahaṃ brahman kathaṃ saṅgo ghaṭeta nau ||
5.44.d:
वसिष्ठस्य कुले रम्ये त्वं जातोऽसि महामते ।
निषादजा त्वहं ब्रह्मन् कथं सङ्गो घटेत नौ ॥
5.44.m: You are born in the delightful lineage of Vasiṣṭha, O wise one; / but I am born of a Niṣāda, O brahmin! How could a union occur between us?

5.44.s:
durlabhaṃ mānuṣaṃ janma brāhmaṇatvaṃ viśeṣataḥ |
tatrāpi tāpasatvaṃ ca durlabhaṃ munisattama ||
5.44.d:
दुर्लभं मानुषं जन्म ब्राह्मणत्वं विशेषतः ।
तत्रापि तापसत्वं च दुर्लभं मुनिसत्तम ॥
5.44.m: Human birth is hard to attain, especially the status of a brahmin; / and even there, the status of an ascetic is hard to attain, O best of sages!

5.44.s:
vidyayā vapuṣā vācā kulaśīlena cānvitaḥ |
kāmabāṇavaśaṃ yāto mahadāścaryamatra hi ||
5.44.d:
विद्यया वपुषा वाचा कुलशीलेन चान्वितः ।
कामबाणवशं यातो महदाश्चर्यमत्र हि ॥
5.44.m: Endowed with learning, a fine form, speech, noble birth, and good conduct, / you have fallen under the sway of the arrows of desire! Great indeed is the wonder here.

5.44.s:
pravṛttamapyasatkarma kartumenaṃ na ko'pi ha |
bhuvi vārayituṃ śaktaḥ śāpabhītyāsya yoginaḥ ||
5.44.d:
प्रवृत्तमप्यसत्कर्म कर्तुमेनं न कोऽपि ह ।
भुवि वारयितुं शक्तः शापभीत्यास्य योगिनः ॥
5.44.m: Even when he has set out to perform an unrighteous deed, no one on earth / is able to restrain this yogin out of fear of his curse.”

5.44.s:
iti sañcintya hṛdaye nijagāda mahāmunim |
tāvaddhairyaṃ kuru svāminyāvattvāṃ pārayāmi na ||
5.44.d:
इति सञ्चिन्त्य हृदये निजगाद महामुनिम् ।
तावद्धैर्यं कुरु स्वामिन्यावत्त्वां पारयामि न ॥
5.44.m: Reflecting thus in her heart, she said to the great sage: / “Master, maintain your composure for so long as I have not ferried you across.”

5.44.s:
sūta uvāca |
iti śrutvā vacastasyā yogirājaḥ parāśaraḥ |
tatyāja pāṇiṃ tarasā sindhoḥ pāraṃ gataḥ punaḥ ||
5.44.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्या योगिराजः पराशरः ।
तत्याज पाणिं तरसा सिन्धोः पारं गतः पुनः ॥
5.44.m: Sūta said: / Hearing her words, Parāśara, the king of yogins, / quickly released her hand, and then reached the other shore of the river.

5.44.s:
punarjagrāha tāṃ bālāṃ muniṃḥ kāmaprapīḍitaḥ |
kampamānā tu sā bālā tamuvāca dayānidhim ||
5.44.d:
पुनर्जग्राह तां बालां मुनिंः कामप्रपीडितः ।
कम्पमाना तु सा बाला तमुवाच दयानिधिम् ॥
5.44.m: Afflicted by desire, the sage seized the maiden again. / But trembling, the girl said to that treasury of compassion:

5.44.s:
durgandhāhaṃ muniśreṣṭha kṛṣṇavarṇā niṣādajā |
bhavāṃstu paramodāravicāro yogisattamaḥ ||
5.44.d:
दुर्गन्धाहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ कृष्णवर्णा निषादजा ।
भवांस्तु परमोदारविचारो योगिसत्तमः ॥
5.44.m: “I am foul-smelling, dark-complexioned, and born of a Niṣāda, O best of sages! / You, however, are the best of yogins, whose thoughts are exceedingly noble.

5.44.s:
nāvayorghaṭate saṅgo kācakāñcanayoriva |
tulyajātyākṛtikayoḥ saṅgaḥ saukhyaprado bhavet ||
5.44.d:
नावयोर्घटते सङ्गो काचकाञ्चनयोरिव ।
तुल्यजात्याकृतिकयोः सङ्गः सौख्यप्रदो भवेत् ॥
5.44.m: Union between us is not fitting, like that of glass and gold. / A union between two of equal caste and form brings happiness.

5.44.s:
ityuktena tayā tena kṣaṇamātreṇa kāminī |
kṛtā yojanagandhā tu ramyarūpā manoramā ||
5.44.d:
इत्युक्तेन तया तेन क्षणमात्रेण कामिनी ।
कृता योजनगन्धा तु रम्यरूपा मनोरमा ॥
5.44.m: Addressed thus by her, in merely a moment that desirable woman / was made by him into one fragrant for a yojana, charming in form, and delightful.

5.44.s:
punarjagrāha tāṃ bālāṃ sa muniḥ kāmapīḍitaḥ |
grahītukāmaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā punaḥ provāca vāsavī ||
5.44.d:
पुनर्जग्राह तां बालां स मुनिः कामपीडितः ।
ग्रहीतुकामं तं दृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रोवाच वासवी ॥
5.44.m: Afflicted by desire, the sage seized the girl again. / Seeing him desiring to take hold of her, Vāsavī spoke again:

5.44.s:
rātrau vyavāyaḥ kartavyo na diveti śrutirjagau |
divāsaṅge mahāndoṣo nindā cāpi durāsadā ||
5.44.d:
रात्रौ व्यवायः कर्तव्यो न दिवेति श्रुतिर्जगौ ।
दिवासङ्गे महान्दोषो निन्दा चापि दुरासदा ॥
5.44.m: “Sexual union is to be performed at night, not by day—so proclaims the sacred tradition; / there is great fault in union by day, and difficult-to-endure reproach as well.

5.44.s:
tasmāttāvatpratīkṣasva yāvadbhavati yāminī |
paśyanti mānavāścātra pitā me ca taṭe sthitaḥ ||
5.44.d:
तस्मात्तावत्प्रतीक्षस्व यावद्भवति यामिनी ।
पश्यन्ति मानवाश्चात्र पिता मे च तटे स्थितः ॥
5.44.m: Therefore, wait until night comes; / people are watching here, and my father stands on the bank.”

5.44.s:
tayoktamidamākarṇya vacanaṃ munipuṅgavaḥ |
nīhāraṃ kalpayāmāsa sadyaḥ puṇyabalena vai ||
5.44.d:
तयोक्तमिदमाकर्ण्य वचनं मुनिपुङ्गवः ।
नीहारं कल्पयामास सद्यः पुण्यबलेन वै ॥
5.44.m: Hearing these words spoken by her, the bull among sages / immediately created a mist by the power of his merit.

5.44.s:
nīhāre ca samutpanne tamasā rātrisannibhe |
vyavāyacakitā bālā punaḥ provāca taṃ munim ||
5.44.d:
नीहारे च समुत्पन्ने तमसा रात्रिसन्निभे ।
व्यवायचकिता बाला पुनः प्रोवाच तं मुनिम् ॥
5.44.m: When the mist arose, resembling the night with darkness, / the maiden, startled by sexual union, spoke again to the sage:

5.44.s:
yoginnamoghavīryastvaṃ bhuktvā gantāsi māṃ yadi |
sagarbhā syāṃ tadā svāminkā gatirme bhavediti ||
5.44.d:
योगिन्नमोघवीर्यस्त्वं भुक्त्वा गन्तासि मां यदि ।
सगर्भा स्यां तदा स्वामिन्का गतिर्मे भवेदिति ॥
5.44.m: “O yogin, your semen is unfailing; if you depart after enjoying me, / I may become pregnant; then, master, what will become of me?

5.44.s:
kanyāvrataṃ mahābuddhe mama naṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati |
hasiṣyanti tadā lokāḥ pitaraṃ kiṃ bravīmyaham ||
5.44.d:
कन्याव्रतं महाबुद्धे मम नष्टं भविष्यति ।
हसिष्यन्ति तदा लोकाः पितरं किं ब्रवीम्यहम् ॥
5.44.m: My maidenhood will be ruined, O one of great intellect; / then people will laugh, and what shall I say to my father?”

5.44.s:
parāśara uvāca |
rama bāle mayā sārdhaṃ svacchandaṃ kāmajai rasaiḥ |
svīyābhilāṣamākhyāhi pūrayāmyadhunā priye ||
5.44.d:
पराशर उवाच ।
रम बाले मया सार्धं स्वच्छन्दं कामजै रसैः ।
स्वीयाभिलाषमाख्याहि पूरयाम्यधुना प्रिये ॥
5.44.m: Parāśara said: / “Sport with me freely, O girl, with the delights born of love! / Tell me your desire; I shall fulfill it now, my dear.

5.44.s:
madājñāsatyakaraṇānnāmnā satyavatī bhava |
vandanīyā tathāśeṣairyogibhistridaśairapi ||
5.44.d:
मदाज्ञासत्यकरणान्नाम्ना सत्यवती भव ।
वन्दनीया तथाशेषैर्योगिभिस्त्रिदशैरपि ॥
5.44.m: Because you have made my command come true, be named Satyavatī; / and you shall be revered by all yogins and even the gods.”

5.44.s:
satyavatyuvāca |
jānate na pitā mātā na vānye bhuvi mānavāḥ |
kanyādharmo na me hanyādyadi svīkuru māṃ tadā ||
5.44.d:
सत्यवत्युवाच ।
जानते न पिता माता न वान्ये भुवि मानवाः ।
कन्याधर्मो न मे हन्याद्यदि स्वीकुरु मां तदा ॥
5.44.m: Satyavatī said: / “Neither father, mother, nor other mortals on earth must know of it, / nor should my status as a maiden be destroyed; if so, accept me then.

5.44.s:
putraśca tvatsamo nātha bhavedadbhutaśaktimān |
saugandhyaṃ sarvadāṅge me tāruṇyaṃ ca navaṃ navam ||
5.44.d:
पुत्रश्च त्वत्समो नाथ भवेदद्भुतशक्तिमान् ।
सौगन्ध्यं सर्वदाङ्गे मे तारुण्यं च नवं नवम् ॥
5.44.m: And may a son be born equal to you, O lord, possessing wondrous power; / may fragrance forever be on my body, and my youth ever fresh.”

5.44.s:
parāśara uvāca |
śṛṇu priye tavābhīṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhaviṣyati |
viṣṇvaṃśasambhavaḥ putro bhavitā te mahāyaśāḥ ||
5.44.d:
पराशर उवाच ।
शृणु प्रिये तवाभीष्टं सर्वं पूर्णं भविष्यति ।
विष्ण्वंशसम्भवः पुत्रो भविता ते महायशाः ॥
5.44.m: Parāśara said: / “Listen, my dear: all that you desire shall be fulfilled; / your son, born of a portion of Viṣṇu, will possess great renown.

5.44.s:
kiñcidvai kāraṇaṃ viddhi yato'haṃ kāmapīḍitaḥ |
dṛṣṭvā cāpsarasāṃ rūpaṃ nāmuhyanme manaḥ kvacit ||
5.44.d:
किञ्चिद्वै कारणं विद्धि यतोऽहं कामपीडितः ।
दृष्ट्वा चाप्सरसां रूपं नामुह्यन्मे मनः क्वचित् ॥
5.44.m: Know that there is some cause whereby I am afflicted with desire; / even upon seeing the beauty of apsarases, my mind was never bewildered anywhere.

5.44.s:
mīnagandhāṃ samālakṣya tvāṃ mohavaśago'bhavam |
na bāle bhālapaṭṭastho brahmalekho'nyathā bhavet ||
5.44.d:
मीनगन्धां समालक्ष्य त्वां मोहवशगोऽभवम् ।
न बाले भालपट्टस्थो ब्रह्मलेखोऽन्यथा भवेत् ॥
5.44.m: Perceiving you, smelling of fish, I fell under the sway of delusion; / O girl, the writing of Brahmā inscribed on the forehead cannot be otherwise.

5.44.s:
purāṇakartā putraste vedaśākhāvibhāgakṛt |
bhaviṣyati varārohe khyātakīrtirjagattraye ||
5.44.d:
पुराणकर्ता पुत्रस्ते वेदशाखाविभागकृत् ।
भविष्यति वरारोहे ख्यातकीर्तिर्जगत्त्रये ॥
5.44.m: Your son will be the author of the Purāṇas and the divider of the branches of the Veda, / and he will be of renowned fame in the three worlds, O woman of lovely limbs!”

5.44.s:
ityuktvā tāṃ suramyāṅgīṃ bhuktvā yogaviśāradaḥ |
vavrāja śīghraṃ yamunājale snātvā mahāmune ||
5.44.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तां सुरम्याङ्गीं भुक्त्वा योगविशारदः ।
वव्राज शीघ्रं यमुनाजले स्नात्वा महामुने ॥
5.44.m: Having spoken thus and enjoyed that woman of lovely limbs, the expert in yoga / quickly departed after bathing in the waters of the Yamunā, O great sage.

5.44.s:
sāpi garbhaṃ dadhārāśu dvādaśātmasamaprabham |
asūta sūryajādvīpe kāmadevamivātmajam ||
5.44.d:
सापि गर्भं दधाराशु द्वादशात्मसमप्रभम् ।
असूत सूर्यजाद्वीपे कामदेवमिवात्मजम् ॥
5.44.m: She too quickly conceived an embryo with a splendor equal to the sun; / on the island in the Yamunā, she gave birth to a son who was like Kāmadeva,

5.44.s:
vāme kamaṇḍaluṃ bibhraddakṣiṇe daṇḍamuttamam |
piśaṅgībhirjaṭābhiśca rājito mahasāṃ cayaḥ ||
5.44.d:
वामे कमण्डलुं बिभ्रद्दक्षिणे दण्डमुत्तमम् ।
पिशङ्गीभिर्जटाभिश्च राजितो महसां चयः ॥
5.44.m: holding a water pot in his left hand and an excellent staff in his right, / resplendent with reddish-brown matted locks, a mass of splendors.

5.44.s:
jātamātrastu tejasvī mātaraṃ pratyabhāṣata |
gaccha mātaryathākāmaṃ gacchāmyahamataḥ param ||
5.44.d:
जातमात्रस्तु तेजस्वी मातरं प्रत्यभाषत ।
गच्छ मातर्यथाकामं गच्छाम्यहमतः परम् ॥
5.44.m: As soon as he was born, the radiant one addressed his mother: / “Go, mother, according to your pleasure; henceforth I shall go.

5.44.s:
mātaryadā bhavetkāryaṃ tava kiñcid hṛdīpsitam |
saṃsmṛtaścāgamiṣyāmi tvadicchāpūrtihetave ||
5.44.d:
मातर्यदा भवेत्कार्यं तव किञ्चिद् हृदीप्सितम् ।
संस्मृतश्चागमिष्यामि त्वदिच्छापूर्तिहेतवे ॥
5.44.m: O mother, whenever any purpose desired in your heart should arise, / I will come when remembered, in order to fulfill your wish.”

5.44.s:
ityuktvā mātṛcaraṇāvabhivādya taponidhiḥ |
jagāma ca tapaḥ kartuṃ tīrthaṃ pāpaviśodhanam ||
5.44.d:
इत्युक्त्वा मातृचरणावभिवाद्य तपोनिधिः ।
जगाम च तपः कर्तुं तीर्थं पापविशोधनम् ॥
5.44.m: Having spoken thus and bowed to his mother’s feet, that treasure of austerity / went to a holy site that purifies sins, in order to perform austerity.

5.44.s:
sāpi pitrantikaṃ yātā putrasnehākulā satī |
smarantī caritaṃ sūnorvarṇayantī svabhāgyakam ||
5.44.d:
सापि पित्रन्तिकं याता पुत्रस्नेहाकुला सती ।
स्मरन्ती चरितं सूनोर्वर्णयन्ती स्वभाग्यकम् ॥
5.44.m: She too went to her father’s presence, the virtuous woman agitated with affection for her son, / remembering the conduct of her son and extolling her good fortune.

5.44.s:
dvīpe jāto yato bālastena dvaipāyano'bhavat |
vedaśākhāvibhajanādvedavyāsaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
5.44.d:
द्वीपे जातो यतो बालस्तेन द्वैपायनोऽभवत् ।
वेदशाखाविभजनाद्वेदव्यासः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
5.44.m: Because the boy was born on an island, he became Dvaipāyana; / because he divided the branches of the Veda, he was celebrated as Vedavyāsa.

5.44.s:
tīrtharājaṃ prathamato dharmakāmārthamokṣadam |
naimiṣaṃ ca kurukṣetraṃ gaṅgādvāramavantikām ||
5.44.d:
तीर्थराजं प्रथमतो धर्मकामार्थमोक्षदम् ।
नैमिषं च कुरुक्षेत्रं गङ्गाद्वारमवन्तिकाम् ॥
5.44.m: First to Prayāga, which grants virtue, pleasure, wealth, and liberation; / to Naimiṣa, Kurukṣetra, Gaṅgādvāra, and Avantikā;

5.44.s:
ayodhyāṃ mathurāṃ caiva dvārakāmamarāvatīm |
sarasvatīṃ sindhusaṅgaṃ gaṅgāsāgarasaṅgamam ||
5.44.d:
अयोध्यां मथुरां चैव द्वारकाममरावतीम् ।
सरस्वतीं सिन्धुसङ्गं गङ्गासागरसङ्गमम् ॥
5.44.m: to Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Dvārakā, and Amarāvatī; / to the Sarasvatī, the confluence of the Indus, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean;

5.44.s:
kāñcīṃ ca tryambakaṃ cāpi saptagodāvarītaṭam |
kālañjaraṃ prabhāsaṃ ca tathā badarikāśramam ||
5.44.d:
काञ्चीं च त्र्यम्बकं चापि सप्तगोदावरीतटम् ।
कालञ्जरं प्रभासं च तथा बदरिकाश्रमम् ॥
5.44.m: to Kāñcī, Tryambaka, and the bank of the Saptagodāvarī; / to Kālañjara, Prabhāsa, and likewise Badarikāśrama;

5.44.s:
mahālayaṃ tathoṅkārakṣetraṃ vai puruṣottamam |
gokarṇaṃ bhṛgukacchaṃ ca bhṛgutuṅgaṃ ca puṣkaram ||
5.44.d:
महालयं तथोङ्कारक्षेत्रं वै पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
गोकर्णं भृगुकच्छं च भृगुतुङ्गं च पुष्करम् ॥
5.44.m: to Mahālaya, the field of Oṅkāra, Puruṣottama, / Gokarṇa, Bhṛgukaccha, Bhṛgutuṅga, and Puṣkara;

5.44.s:
śrīparvatāditīrthāni dhārātīrthaṃ tathaiva ca |
gatvāvagāhya vidhinā cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ ||
5.44.d:
श्रीपर्वतादितीर्थानि धारातीर्थं तथैव च ।
गत्वावगाह्य विधिना चचार परमं तपः ॥
5.44.m: having gone to holy places such as Śrīparvata and likewise Dhārātīrtha / and having bathed according to rule, he performed supreme austerity.

5.44.s:
evaṃ tīrthānyanekāni nānādeśasthitāni ha |
paryaṭankālikāsūnuḥ prāpadvārāṇasīṃ purīm ||
5.44.d:
एवं तीर्थान्यनेकानि नानादेशस्थितानि ह ।
पर्यटन्कालिकासूनुः प्रापद्वाराणसीं पुरीम् ॥
5.44.m: Thus, wandering through many holy places situated in various regions, / the son of Kālikā reached the city of Vārāṇasī,

5.44.s:
yatra viśveśvaraḥ sākṣādannapūrṇā maheśvarī |
bhaktānāmamṛtaṃ dātuṃ virājete kṛpānidhī ||
5.44.d:
यत्र विश्वेश्वरः साक्षादन्नपूर्णा महेश्वरी ।
भक्तानाममृतं दातुं विराजेते कृपानिधी ॥
5.44.m: where Viśveśvara in person and Maheśvarī Annapūrṇā, / those two treasuries of mercy, shine resplendent to grant nectar to devotees.

5.44.s:
prāpya vārāṇasītīrthaṃ dṛṣṭvātha maṇikarṇikām |
koṭijanmārjitaṃ pāpaṃ tatyāja sa munīśvaraḥ ||
5.44.d:
प्राप्य वाराणसीतीर्थं दृष्ट्वाथ मणिकर्णिकाम् ।
कोटिजन्मार्जितं पापं तत्याज स मुनीश्वरः ॥
5.44.m: Reaching the holy site of Vārāṇasī and then beholding Maṇikarṇikā, / that lord of sages abandoned the sins accumulated through ten million births.

5.44.s:
dṛṣṭvā liṅgāni sarvāṇi viśveśapramukhāni ca |
snātvā sarveṣu kuṇḍeṣu vāpīkūpasaraḥsu ca ||
5.44.d:
दृष्ट्वा लिङ्गानि सर्वाणि विश्वेशप्रमुखानि च ।
स्नात्वा सर्वेषु कुण्डेषु वापीकूपसरःसु च ॥
5.44.m: Having beheld all the liṅgas, headed by Viśveśa, / and having bathed in all the sacred pools, step-wells, wells, and lakes,

5.44.s:
natvā vināyakānsarvāngaurīḥ sarvāḥ praṇamya ca |
sampūjya kālarājaṃ ca bhairavaṃ pāpabhakṣaṇam ||
5.44.d:
नत्वा विनायकान्सर्वान्गौरीः सर्वाः प्रणम्य च ।
सम्पूज्य कालराजं च भैरवं पापभक्षणम् ॥
5.44.m: Having bowed to all the Vināyakas and having paid homage to all the Gaurīs, / and having fully worshipped Kālarāja, the Bhairava who devours sin,

5.44.s:
daṇḍanāyakamukhyāṃśca gaṇānstutvā prayatnataḥ |
ādikeśavamukhyāṃśca keśavānparitoṣya ca ||
5.44.d:
दण्डनायकमुख्यांश्च गणान्स्तुत्वा प्रयत्नतः ।
आदिकेशवमुख्यांश्च केशवान्परितोष्य च ॥
5.44.m: and having diligently praised the attendants headed by Daṇḍanāyaka, / and having pleased the Keśavas headed by Ādikeśava,

5.44.s:
lolārkamukhyasūryāṃśca praṇamya ca punaḥpunaḥ |
kṛtvā piṇḍapradānāni sarvatīrtheṣvatandritaḥ ||
5.44.d:
लोलार्कमुख्यसूर्यांश्च प्रणम्य च पुनःपुनः ।
कृत्वा पिण्डप्रदानानि सर्वतीर्थेष्वतन्द्रितः ॥
5.44.m: and having repeatedly bowed to the suns headed by Lolārka, / and unweariedly offering ancestral balls of rice at all the holy sites,

5.44.s:
sthāpayāmāsa puṇyātmā liṅgaṃ vyāseśvarābhidham |
yaddarśanādbhavedviprā naro vidyāsu vākpatiḥ ||
5.44.d:
स्थापयामास पुण्यात्मा लिङ्गं व्यासेश्वराभिधम् ।
यद्दर्शनाद्भवेद्विप्रा नरो विद्यासु वाक्पतिः ॥
5.44.m: that holy-souled one established a liṅga named Vyāseśvara, / by seeing which, O Brahmins, a man becomes a master of speech in the sciences.

5.44.s:
liṅgānyabhyarcya viśveśapramukhāni subhaktitaḥ |
asakṛccintayāmāsa kiṃ liṅgaṃ kṣiprasiddhidam ||
5.44.d:
लिङ्गान्यभ्यर्च्य विश्वेशप्रमुखानि सुभक्तितः ।
असकृच्चिन्तयामास किं लिङ्गं क्षिप्रसिद्धिदम् ॥
5.44.m: Having worshipped the liṅgas headed by Viśveśa with great devotion, / he repeatedly reflected: 'Which liṅga is it that bestows quick success?

5.44.s:
yamārādhya mahādevaṃ vidyāḥ sarvā labhemahi |
purāṇakartṛtāśaktirmamāstu yadanugrahāt ||
5.44.d:
यमाराध्य महादेवं विद्याः सर्वा लभेमहि ।
पुराणकर्तृताशक्तिर्ममास्तु यदनुग्रहात् ॥
5.44.m: By worshipping which Mahādeva may we attain all the sciences? / By whose favor may the power of authorship of the Purāṇas be mine?

5.44.s:
śrīmadoṅkāranāthaṃ vā kṛttivāseśvaraṃ kimu |
kedāreśaṃ tu kāmeśaṃ candreśaṃ vā trilocanam ||
5.44.d:
श्रीमदोङ्कारनाथं वा कृत्तिवासेश्वरं किमु ।
केदारेशं तु कामेशं चन्द्रेशं वा त्रिलोचनम् ॥
5.44.m: Is it glorious Oṅkāranātha, or perhaps Kṛttivāseśvara, / Kedāreśa, or Kāmeśa, Candreśa, or Trilocana?

5.44.s:
kāleśaṃ vṛddhakāleśaṃ kalaśeśvarameva vā |
jyeṣṭheśaṃ jambukeśaṃ vā jaigīṣavyeśvaraṃ tu vā ||
5.44.d:
कालेशं वृद्धकालेशं कलशेश्वरमेव वा ।
ज्येष्ठेशं जम्बुकेशं वा जैगीषव्येश्वरं तु वा ॥
5.44.m: Kāleśa, Vṛddhakāleśa, or indeed Kalaśeśvara? / Jyeṣṭheśa, or Jambukeśa, or Jaigīṣavyeśvara?

5.44.s:
daśāśvamedhamīśānaṃ drumacaṇḍeśameva vā |
dṛkkeśaṃ garuḍeśaṃ vā gokarṇeśaṃ gaṇeśvaram ||
5.44.d:
दशाश्वमेधमीशानं द्रुमचण्डेशमेव वा ।
दृक्केशं गरुडेशं वा गोकर्णेशं गणेश्वरम् ॥
5.44.m: Daśāśvamedha-Īśāna, or Drumacaṇḍeśa? / Dṛkkeśa, or Garuḍeśa, Gokarṇeśa, or Gaṇeśvara?

5.44.s:
prasannavadaneśaṃ vā dharmeśaṃ tārakeśvaram |
nandikeśaṃ nivāseśaṃ patrīśaṃ prītikeśvaram ||
5.44.d:
प्रसन्नवदनेशं वा धर्मेशं तारकेश्वरम् ।
नन्दिकेशं निवासेशं पत्रीशं प्रीतिकेश्वरम् ॥
5.44.m: Prasannavadaneśa, Dharmeśa, or Tārakeśvara? / Nandikeśa, Nivāseśa, Patrīśa, or Prītikeśvara?

5.44.s:
parvateśaṃ paśupatiṃ hāṭakeśvarameva vā |
bṛhaspatīśvaraṃ vātha tilabhāṇḍeśameva vā ||
5.44.d:
पर्वतेशं पशुपतिं हाटकेश्वरमेव वा ।
बृहस्पतीश्वरं वाथ तिलभाण्डेशमेव वा ॥
5.44.m: Parvateśa, Paśupati, or Hāṭakeśvara? / Bṛhaspatīśvara, or indeed Tilabhāṇḍeśa?

5.44.s:
bhārabhūteśvaraṃ kiṃ vā mahālakṣmīśvaraṃ tu vā |
maruteśaṃ tu mokṣeśaṃ gaṅgeśaṃ narmadeśvaram ||
5.44.d:
भारभूतेश्वरं किं वा महालक्ष्मीश्वरं तु वा ।
मरुतेशं तु मोक्षेशं गङ्गेशं नर्मदेश्वरम् ॥
5.44.m: Is it Bhārabhūteśvara, or Mahālakṣmīśvara? / Maruteśa, Mokṣeśa, Gaṅgeśa, or Narmadeśvara?

5.44.s:
kṛṣṇeśaṃ parameśānaṃ ratneśvaramathāpi vā |
yāmuneśaṃ lāṅgalīśaṃ śrīmadviśveśvaraṃ vibhum ||
5.44.d:
कृष्णेशं परमेशानं रत्नेश्वरमथापि वा ।
यामुनेशं लाङ्गलीशं श्रीमद्विश्वेश्वरं विभुम् ॥
5.44.m: Kṛṣṇeśa, Parameśāna, or Ratneśvara? / Yāmuneśa, Lāṅgalīśa, or the all-pervading, glorious Viśveśvara?

5.44.s:
avimukteśvaraṃ vātha viśālākṣīśameva vā |
vyāghreśvaraṃ varāheśaṃ vidyeśvaramathāpi vā ||
5.44.d:
अविमुक्तेश्वरं वाथ विशालाक्षीशमेव वा ।
व्याघ्रेश्वरं वराहेशं विद्येश्वरमथापि वा ॥
5.44.m: Avimukteśvara, or Viśālākṣīśa? / Vyāghreśvara, Varāheśa, or Vidyeśvara?

5.44.s:
varuṇeśaṃ vidhīśaṃ vā harikeśeśvaraṃ tu vā |
bhavānīśaṃ kapardīśaṃ kandukeśamajeśvaram ||
5.44.d:
वरुणेशं विधीशं वा हरिकेशेश्वरं तु वा ।
भवानीशं कपर्दीशं कन्दुकेशमजेश्वरम् ॥
5.44.m: Varuṇeśa, Vidhīśa, or Harikeśeśvara? / Bhavānīśa, Kapardīśa, Kandukeśa, or Ajeśvara?

5.44.s:
viśvakarmeśvaraṃ vātha vīreśvaramathāpi vā |
nādeśaṃ kapileśaṃ ca bhuvaneśvarameva vā ||
5.44.d:
विश्वकर्मेश्वरं वाथ वीरेश्वरमथापि वा ।
नादेशं कपिलेशं च भुवनेश्वरमेव वा ॥
5.44.m: Viśvakarmeśvara, or Vīreśvara? / Nādeśa, Kapileśa, or Bhuvaneśvara?

5.44.s:
vāṣkulīśaṃ mahādevaṃ siddhīśvaramathāpi vā |
viśvedeveśvaraṃ vīrabhadreśaṃ bhairaveśvaram ||
5.44.d:
वाष्कुलीशं महादेवं सिद्धीश्वरमथापि वा ।
विश्वेदेवेश्वरं वीरभद्रेशं भैरवेश्वरम् ॥
5.44.m: Vāṣkulīśa, Mahādeva, or Siddhīśvara? / Viśvedeveśvara, Vīrabhadreśa, or Bhairaveśvara?

5.44.s:
amṛteśaṃ satīśaṃ vā pārvatīśvarameva vā |
siddheśvaraṃ mataṅgeśaṃ bhūtīśvaramathāpi vā ||
5.44.d:
अमृतेशं सतीशं वा पार्वतीश्वरमेव वा ।
सिद्धेश्वरं मतङ्गेशं भूतीश्वरमथापि वा ॥
5.44.m: Amṛteśa, Satīśa, or Pārvatīśvara? / Siddheśvara, Mataṅgeśa, or Bhūtīśvara?

5.44.s:
āṣāḍhīśaṃ prakāśeśaṃ koṭirudreśvaraṃ tathā |
madālaseśvaraṃ caiva tilaparṇeśvaraṃ kimu ||
5.44.d:
आषाढीशं प्रकाशेशं कोटिरुद्रेश्वरं तथा ।
मदालसेश्वरं चैव तिलपर्णेश्वरं किमु ॥
5.44.m: Āṣāḍhīśa, Prakāśeśa, and Koṭirudreśvara? / Madālaseśvara, or Tilaparṇeśvara?

5.44.s:
kiṃ vā hiraṇyagarbheśaṃ kiṃ vā śrīmadhyameśvaram |
ityādi koṭiliṅgānāṃ madhye'haṃ kimupāśraye ||
5.44.d:
किं वा हिरण्यगर्भेशं किं वा श्रीमध्यमेश्वरम् ।
इत्यादि कोटिलिङ्गानां मध्येऽहं किमुपाश्रये ॥
5.44.m: Is it Hiraṇyagarbheśa, or glorious Madhyameśvara? / Among these and other tens of millions of liṅgas, which one should I resort to?'

5.44.s:
iti cintāturo vyāsaḥ śivabhaktiratātmavān |
kṣaṇaṃ vicārayāmāsa dhyānasusthiracetasā ||
5.44.d:
इति चिन्तातुरो व्यासः शिवभक्तिरतात्मवान् ।
क्षणं विचारयामास ध्यानसुस्थिरचेतसा ॥
5.44.m: Anxious with this thought, Vyāsa, self-controlled and devoted to Śiva, / considered for a moment with a mind made steady in meditation.

5.44.s:
āṃ jñātaṃ vismṛtaṃ tāvanniṣpanno me manorathaḥ |
siddhaiḥ sampūjitaṃ liṅgaṃ dharmakāmārthamokṣadam ||
5.44.d:
आं ज्ञातं विस्मृतं तावन्निष्पन्नो मे मनोरथः ।
सिद्धैः सम्पूजितं लिङ्गं धर्मकामार्थमोक्षदम् ॥
5.44.m: 'Ah, I know! It was forgotten till now, but my wish is fulfilled! / The liṅga worshipped by the Siddhas, which bestows duty, desire, wealth, and liberation;

5.44.s:
darśanātsparśanādyasya ceto nirmalatāmiyāt |
udghāṭitaṃ sadaivāsti dvāraṃ svargasya yatra hi ||
5.44.d:
दर्शनात्स्पर्शनाद्यस्य चेतो निर्मलतामियात् ।
उद्घाटितं सदैवास्ति द्वारं स्वर्गस्य यत्र हि ॥
5.44.m: by seeing and touching which the mind reaches purity; / where the door to heaven is truly open at all times;

5.44.s:
avimukte mahākṣetre siddhakṣetre hi tatparam |
yatrāste paramaṃ liṅgaṃ madhyameśvarasaṃjñakam ||
5.44.d:
अविमुक्ते महाक्षेत्रे सिद्धक्षेत्रे हि तत्परम् ।
यत्रास्ते परमं लिङ्गं मध्यमेश्वरसंज्ञकम् ॥
5.44.m: in the great field of Avimukta, the field of the accomplished, there is that supreme [site], / where the supreme liṅga named Madhyameśvara abides.

5.44.s:
na madhyameśvarādanyālliṅgaṃ kāśyāṃ hi vidyate |
yaddarśanārthamāyānti devāḥ parvaṇi parvaṇi ||
5.44.d:
न मध्यमेश्वरादन्याल्लिङ्गं काश्यां हि विद्यते ।
यद्दर्शनार्थमायान्ति देवाः पर्वणि पर्वणि ॥
5.44.m: Indeed, there is no liṅga in Kāśī other than Madhyameśvara / to see which the gods arrive at every festive occasion.

5.44.s:
ataḥ sevyo mahādevo madhyameśvarasaṃjñakaḥ |
asyārādhanato viprā bahavaḥ siddhimāgatāḥ ||
5.44.d:
अतः सेव्यो महादेवो मध्यमेश्वरसंज्ञकः ।
अस्याराधनतो विप्रा बहवः सिद्धिमागताः ॥
5.44.m: Therefore, Mahādeva named Madhyameśvara is to be served; / from worshipping him, O Brahmins, many have attained perfection.

5.44.s:
yaḥ pradhānatayā kāśyāṃ madhye tiṣṭhati śaṅkaraḥ |
svapurījana saukhyārthamato'sau madhyameśvaraḥ ||
5.44.d:
यः प्रधानतया काश्यां मध्ये तिष्ठति शङ्करः ।
स्वपुरीजन सौख्यार्थमतोऽसौ मध्यमेश्वरः ॥
5.44.m: Because Śaṅkara stands prominently in the center of Kāśī / for the happiness of the people of his city, he is called Madhyameśvara.

5.44.s:
tumbururnāma gandharvo devarṣirnāradastathā |
amumārādhya sampanno gānavidyāviśāradau ||
5.44.d:
तुम्बुरुर्नाम गन्धर्वो देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा ।
अमुमाराध्य सम्पन्नो गानविद्याविशारदौ ॥
5.44.m: The Gandharva named Tumburu and the divine sage Nārada / became skilled in the art of music having worshipped this one.

5.44.s:
amumeva samārādhya viṣṇurmokṣaprado'bhavat |
brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca sṛṣṭipālakahārakāḥ ||
5.44.d:
अमुमेव समाराध्य विष्णुर्मोक्षप्रदोऽभवत् ।
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च सृष्टिपालकहारकाः ॥
5.44.m: Having worshipped this very one, Viṣṇu became the bestower of liberation, / and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra became the creator, preserver, and destroyer.

5.44.s:
dhanādhīśaḥ kubero'pi vāmadevo hi śaivarāṭ |
khaṭvāṅgo nāma bhūpālo'napatyo'patyavānabhūt ||
5.44.d:
धनाधीशः कुबेरोऽपि वामदेवो हि शैवराट् ।
खट्वाङ्गो नाम भूपालोऽनपत्योऽपत्यवानभूत् ॥
5.44.m: Kubera, the lord of wealth, and Vāmadeva, the king of Śaivas, [achieved their ends], / and the childless king named Khaṭvāṅga obtained offspring.

5.44.s:
apsarāścandrabhāmākhyā nṛtyantī nijabhāvataḥ |
sadehā kokilālāpā liṅgamadhye layaṃ gatā ||
5.44.d:
अप्सराश्चन्द्रभामाख्या नृत्यन्ती निजभावतः ।
सदेहा कोकिलालापा लिङ्गमध्ये लयं गता ॥
5.44.m: The celestial nymph named Candrabhāmā, dancing with innate emotion, / cuckoo-voiced, dissolved bodily into the center of the liṅga.

5.44.s:
śrīkaro gopikāsūnuḥ sevitvā madhyameśvaram |
gāṇapatyaṃ samālebhe śivasya karuṇātmanaḥ ||
5.44.d:
श्रीकरो गोपिकासूनुः सेवित्वा मध्यमेश्वरम् ।
गाणपत्यं समालेभे शिवस्य करुणात्मनः ॥
5.44.m: Śrīkara, the son of a cowherdess, having served Madhyameśvara, / obtained lordship of the attendants from compassionate Śiva.

5.44.s:
bhārgavo gīṣpatiścobhau devau daityasurārcitau |
vidyāpāraṅgatau jātau prasādānmadhyameśituḥ ||
5.44.d:
भार्गवो गीष्पतिश्चोभौ देवौ दैत्यसुरार्चितौ ।
विद्यापारङ्गतौ जातौ प्रसादान्मध्यमेशितुः ॥
5.44.m: Bhārgava and Gīṣpati, the two gods worshipped by Daityas and deities, / became masters of the sciences by the grace of Madhyameśvara.

5.44.s:
ahamapyatra sampūjya madhyameśvaramīśvaram |
purāṇakartṛtāśaktiṃ prāpsyāmi tarasā dhruvam ||
5.44.d:
अहमप्यत्र सम्पूज्य मध्यमेश्वरमीश्वरम् ।
पुराणकर्तृताशक्तिं प्राप्स्यामि तरसा ध्रुवम् ॥
5.44.m: I too, having worshipped Lord Madhyameśvara here, / shall surely and swiftly attain the power of Purāṇa authorship.'

5.44.s:
iti kṛtvā matiṃ dhīro vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ |
bhāgīrathyambhasi snātvā jagrāha niyamaṃ vratī ||
5.44.d:
इति कृत्वा मतिं धीरो व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः ।
भागीरथ्यम्भसि स्नात्वा जग्राह नियमं व्रती ॥
5.44.m: Having resolved thus, the steadfast Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, / bathed in the waters of the Bhāgīrathī and took up his vows as an ascetic.

5.44.s:
kvacitparṇāśano bhūttvā phalaśākāśanaḥ kvacit |
vātabhugjalabhuk kvāpi kvacinniraśanavratī ||
5.44.d:
क्वचित्पर्णाशनो भूत्त्वा फलशाकाशनः क्वचित् ।
वातभुग्जलभुक् क्वापि क्वचिन्निरशनव्रती ॥
5.44.m: Sometimes eating leaves, sometimes eating fruits and vegetables, / somewhere feeding on wind, drinking water somewhere, and at times fasting,

5.44.s:
ityādiniyamairyogī trikālaṃ madhyameśvaram |
pūjayāmāsa dharmātmā nānāvṛkṣodbhavaiḥ phalaiḥ ||
5.44.d:
इत्यादिनियमैर्योगी त्रिकालं मध्यमेश्वरम् ।
पूजयामास धर्मात्मा नानावृक्षोद्भवैः फलैः ॥
5.44.m: the righteous yogi worshipped Madhyameśvara at the three twilights / through such observances with fruits born of various trees.

5.44.s:
itthaṃ bahutithe kāle vyatīte kālikāsutaḥ |
snātvā tripathagātoye yāvadāyāti sa prage ||
5.44.d:
इत्थं बहुतिथे काले व्यतीते कालिकासुतः ।
स्नात्वा त्रिपथगातोये यावदायाति स प्रगे ॥
5.44.m: When a long time had thus passed, the son of Kālikā, / having bathed in the water of the three-streamed river, as he arrived in the morning

5.44.s:
madhyameśvaramīśānaṃ bhaktābhīṣṭavarapradam |
tāvaddadarśa puṇyātmā madhye liṅgaṃ maheśvaram ||
5.44.d:
मध्यमेश्वरमीशानं भक्ताभीष्टवरप्रदम् ।
तावद्ददर्श पुण्यात्मा मध्ये लिङ्गं महेश्वरम् ॥
5.44.m: to Madhyameśvara, the Lord who grants the desired boons of his devotees, / the virtuous one saw Maheśvara within the liṅga:

5.44.s:
umābhūṣitavāmāṅgaṃ vyāghracarmottarīyakam |
jaṭājūṭacaladgaṅgātaraṅgaiścāruvigraham ||
lasacchāradabālenducandrikācandritālakam |
bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgaṃ karpūrārjunavigraham ||
5.44.d:
उमाभूषितवामाङ्गं व्याघ्रचर्मोत्तरीयकम् ।
जटाजूटचलद्गङ्गातरङ्गैश्चारुविग्रहम् ॥
लसच्छारदबालेन्दुचन्द्रिकाचन्द्रितालकम् ।
भस्मोद्धूलितसर्वाङ्गं कर्पूरार्जुनविग्रहम् ॥
5.44.m:
his left side adorned by Umā, his upper garment a tiger skin, / his form lovely with the waves of the Gaṅgā rippling in his matted hair;

his locks brightened by the moonlight of the shining autumn crescent moon, / his entire body smeared with ashes, his form white as camphor;

5.44.s:
karṇāntāyatanetraṃ ca vidrumāruṇadacchadam |
pañcavarṣākṛtiṃ bālaṃ bālakocitabhūṣaṇam ||
5.44.d:
कर्णान्तायतनेत्रं च विद्रुमारुणदच्छदम् ।
पञ्चवर्षाकृतिं बालं बालकोचितभूषणम् ॥
5.44.m: his eyes elongated to the ends of his ears, his lips red like coral, / having the form of a five-year-old child, wearing ornaments fitting a boy;

5.44.s:
dadhānaṃ koṭikandarpadarpahāniṃ tanudyutim |
nagraṃ prahasitāsyābjaṃ gāyantaṃ sāma līlayā ||
5.44.d:
दधानं कोटिकन्दर्पदर्पहानिं तनुद्युतिम् ।
नग्रं प्रहसितास्याब्जं गायन्तं साम लीलया ॥
5.44.m: bearing bodily radiance that destroys the pride of ten million love-gods, / naked, his lotus face laughing gently, playfully singing the Sāma;

5.44.s:
karuṇāpārapāthodhiṃ bhaktavatsalanāmakam |
āśutoṣamumākāntaṃ prasādasumukhaṃ haram ||
5.44.d:
करुणापारपाथोधिं भक्तवत्सलनामकम् ।
आशुतोषमुमाकान्तं प्रसादसुमुखं हरम् ॥
5.44.m: a shoreless ocean of compassion, named Affectionate toward Devotees, / easily pleased, Umā's beloved, Hara with a gracious countenance.

5.44.s:
samālokya stutiṃ cakre premagadgadayā girā |
yogināmapyagamyaṃ taṃ dīnabandhuṃ cidātmakam ||
5.44.d:
समालोक्य स्तुतिं चक्रे प्रेमगद्गदया गिरा ।
योगिनामप्यगम्यं तं दीनबन्धुं चिदात्मकम् ॥
5.44.m: Having beheld him, who is inaccessible even to yogis, the friend of the humble, whose essence is consciousness, / he uttered praise with a voice faltering with love.

5.44.s:
vedavyāsa uvāca |
devadeva mahābhāga śaraṇāgatavatsala |
vāṅmanaḥkarmaduṣprāpa yogināmapyagocara ||
5.44.d:
वेदव्यास उवाच ।
देवदेव महाभाग शरणागतवत्सल ।
वाङ्मनःकर्मदुष्प्राप योगिनामप्यगोचर ॥
5.44.m: Vedavyāsa said: / 'O God of gods, O exalted one, O affectionate to those who seek refuge, / hard to reach through speech, mind, and action, beyond the range even of yogis!

5.44.s:
mahimānaṃ na te vedā vidāmāsurumāpate |
tvameva jagataḥ kartā dhartā hartā tathaiva ca ||
5.44.d:
महिमानं न ते वेदा विदामासुरुमापते ।
त्वमेव जगतः कर्ता धर्ता हर्ता तथैव च ॥
5.44.m: The Vedas did not know your greatness, O Lord of Umā! / You alone are the creator, the sustainer, and likewise the destroyer of the universe.

5.44.s:
tvamādyaḥ sarvadevānāṃ saccidānanda īśvaraḥ |
nāmagotre na vā te staḥ sarvajño'si sadāśiva ||
5.44.d:
त्वमाद्यः सर्वदेवानां सच्चिदानन्द ईश्वरः ।
नामगोत्रे न वा ते स्तः सर्वज्ञोऽसि सदाशिव ॥
5.44.m: You are the primal God of all deities, existence-consciousness-bliss, the Lord; / you have neither name nor lineage; you are omniscient, O Sadāśiva!'

5.44.s:
tvameva paramaṃ brahma māyāpāśanivartakaḥ |
guṇatrayairna liptastvaṃ padmapatramivāmbhasā ||
5.44.d:
त्वमेव परमं ब्रह्म मायापाशनिवर्तकः ।
गुणत्रयैर्न लिप्तस्त्वं पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
5.44.m: You alone are the supreme Brahman, the remover of the fetters of illusion. / You are untouched by the three qualities, as a lotus leaf by water.

5.44.s:
na te janma na vā śīlaṃ na deśo na kulaṃ ca te |
itthambhūto'pīśvarastvaṃ trilokyāḥ kāmamāvaheḥ ||
5.44.d:
न ते जन्म न वा शीलं न देशो न कुलं च ते ।
इत्थम्भूतोऽपीश्वरस्त्वं त्रिलोक्याः काममावहेः ॥
5.44.m: You have neither birth nor fixed conduct, neither native country nor family. / Even being such, you, the Lord, fulfill the desires of the three worlds.

5.44.s:
na brahmā na ca lakṣmīśo na ca sendrā divaukasaḥ |
na yogīndrā vidustattvaṃ yasya taṃ tvāmupāsmahe ||
5.44.d:
न ब्रह्मा न च लक्ष्मीशो न च सेन्द्रा दिवौकसः ।
न योगीन्द्रा विदुस्तत्त्वं यस्य तं त्वामुपास्महे ॥
5.44.m: Neither Brahmā, nor the lord of Lakṣmī, nor the gods led by Indra, / nor the lords of yoga know your true nature; we worship you, who are that very one.

5.44.s:
tvattaḥ sarvaṃ tvaṃ hi sarvaṃ gaurīśastvaṃ purāntakaḥ |
tvaṃ bālastvaṃ yuvā vṛddhastaṃ tvāṃ hṛdi yunajmyaham ||
5.44.d:
त्वत्तः सर्वं त्वं हि सर्वं गौरीशस्त्वं पुरान्तकः ।
त्वं बालस्त्वं युवा वृद्धस्तं त्वां हृदि युनज्म्यहम् ॥
5.44.m: Everything comes from you; you indeed are everything, the lord of Gaurī, the destroyer of the [demon] cities. / You are the child, you are the youth, you are the old man; you I bind within my heart.

5.44.s:
namastasmai maheśāya bhaktadhyeyāya śambhave |
purāṇapuruṣāyāddhā śaṅkarāya parātmane ||
5.44.d:
नमस्तस्मै महेशाय भक्तध्येयाय शम्भवे ।
पुराणपुरुषायाद्धा शङ्कराय परात्मने ॥
5.44.m: Salutations to that Maheśa, Śambhu, who is to be meditated upon by devotees, / to the ancient Person indeed, Śaṅkara, the supreme Self.

5.44.s:
iti stutvā kṣitau yāvaddaṇḍavannipapāta saḥ |
tāvatsa bālo hṛṣṭātmā vedavyāsamabhāṣata ||
5.44.d:
इति स्तुत्वा क्षितौ यावद्दण्डवन्निपपात सः ।
तावत्स बालो हृष्टात्मा वेदव्यासमभाषत ॥
5.44.m: Having thus praised him, as soon as he fell prostrate like a staff upon the ground, / just then the child, glad at heart, spoke to Vedavyāsa:

5.44.s:
varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bho yoginyaste manasi vartate |
nādeyaṃ vidyate kiñcidbhaktādhīno yato'smyaham ||
5.44.d:
वरं वृणीष्व भो योगिन्यस्ते मनसि वर्तते ।
नादेयं विद्यते किञ्चिद्भक्ताधीनो यतोऽस्म्यहम् ॥
5.44.m: "O yogin, choose the boon that lies in your mind. / There is nothing that cannot be granted, since I am subject to my devotees."

5.44.s:
tata utthāya hṛṣṭātmā munirvyāso mahātapāḥ |
pratyabravītkimajñātaṃ sarvajñasya tava prabho ||
5.44.d:
तत उत्थाय हृष्टात्मा मुनिर्व्यासो महातपाः ।
प्रत्यब्रवीत्किमज्ञातं सर्वज्ञस्य तव प्रभो ॥
5.44.m: Then, having risen, glad at heart, the sage Vyāsa of great austerities / replied: "What is unknown to you, the all-knowing Lord?

5.44.s:
sarvāntarātmā bhagavān śarvaḥ sarvaprado bhavān |
yāñcāṃ pratiniyuṅkte māṃ kimīśo dainyakāriṇīm ||
5.44.d:
सर्वान्तरात्मा भगवान् शर्वः सर्वप्रदो भवान् ।
याञ्चां प्रतिनियुङ्क्ते मां किमीशो दैन्यकारिणीम् ॥
5.44.m: You are the inner Self of all, the Blessed Lord, Śarva, the giver of everything. / Why does the Lord urge me to make a request, which causes humiliation?"

5.44.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya vyāsasyāmalacetasaḥ |
śuci smitvā mahādevo bālarūpadharo'bravīt ||
5.44.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य व्यासस्यामलचेतसः ।
शुचि स्मित्वा महादेवो बालरूपधरोऽब्रवीत् ॥
5.44.m: Having heard those words of that pure-minded Vyāsa, / smiling gently, Mahādeva, who had assumed the form of a child, spoke:

5.44.s:
bāla uvāca |
tvayā brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭha yo'bhilāṣaḥ kṛto hṛdi |
acireṇaiva kālena sa bhaviṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ ||
5.44.d:
बाल उवाच ।
त्वया ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठ योऽभिलाषः कृतो हृदि ।
अचिरेणैव कालेन स भविष्यत्यसंशयः ॥
5.44.m: The child said: / "O best among knowers of Brahman, the desire you formed in your heart / shall be fulfilled without delay, beyond any doubt.

5.44.s:
kaṇṭhe sthitvā tava brahmannantaryāmyahamīśvaraḥ |
setihāsapurāṇāni samyaṅnirmāpayāmyaham ||
5.44.d:
कण्ठे स्थित्वा तव ब्रह्मन्नन्तर्याम्यहमीश्वरः ।
सेतिहासपुराणानि सम्यङ्निर्मापयाम्यहम् ॥
5.44.m: Abiding in your throat, O brahmin, I, the inner controller, the Lord, / shall cause the Purāṇas along with the Itihāsas to be composed properly.

5.44.s:
abhilāṣāṣṭakaṃ puṇyaṃ stotrametattvayeritam |
varṣaṃ trikālaṃ paṭhanātkāmadaṃ śambhusadmani ||
5.44.d:
अभिलाषाष्टकं पुण्यं स्तोत्रमेतत्त्वयेरितम् ।
वर्षं त्रिकालं पठनात्कामदं शम्भुसद्मनि ॥
5.44.m: This holy hymn, the 'Octad of Desires,' was uttered by you. / Through reciting it at the three daily twilights for a year in the abode of Śambhu, it grants desires.

5.44.s:
etatstotrasya paṭhanaṃ vidyābuddhivivardhanam |
sarvasampatkaraṃ proktaṃ dharmadaṃ mokṣadaṃ nṛṇām ||
5.44.d:
एतत्स्तोत्रस्य पठनं विद्याबुद्धिविवर्धनम् ।
सर्वसम्पत्करं प्रोक्तं धर्मदं मोक्षदं नृणाम् ॥
5.44.m: The recitation of this hymn increases learning and intellect; / it is declared to bestow all prosperity, and to grant virtue and liberation to men.

5.44.s:
prātarutthāya susnāto liṅgamabhyarcya śāṅkaram |
varṣaṃ paṭhannidaṃ stotraṃ mūrkho'pi syād bṛhaspatiḥ ||
5.44.d:
प्रातरुत्थाय सुस्नातो लिङ्गमभ्यर्च्य शाङ्करम् ।
वर्षं पठन्निदं स्तोत्रं मूर्खोऽपि स्याद् बृहस्पतिः ॥
5.44.m: Having risen at dawn and bathed well, having worshipped the liṅga of Śaṅkara / and reciting this hymn for a year, even a fool would become a Bṛhaspati.

5.44.s:
striyā vā puruṣeṇāpi niyamālliṅgasannidhau |
varṣaṃ japtamidaṃ stotraṃ buddhiṃ vidyāṃ ca vardhayet ||
5.44.d:
स्त्रिया वा पुरुषेणापि नियमाल्लिङ्गसन्निधौ ।
वर्षं जप्तमिदं स्तोत्रं बुद्धिं विद्यां च वर्धयेत् ॥
5.44.m: Repeated with self-restraint near a liṅga for a year / by a woman or by a man, this hymn increases intellect and learning."

5.44.s:
ityuktvā sa mahādevo bālo liṅge nyalīyata |
vyāso'pi muñcannaśrūṇi śivapremākulo'bhavat ||
5.44.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स महादेवो बालो लिङ्गे न्यलीयत ।
व्यासोऽपि मुञ्चन्नश्रूणि शिवप्रेमाकुलोऽभवत् ॥
5.44.m: Having spoken thus, that Mahādeva as a child vanished into the liṅga; / and Vyāsa, shedding tears, became overwhelmed with love for Śiva.

5.44.s:
evaṃ labdhavaro vyāso maheśānmadhyameśvarāt |
aṣṭādaśa purāṇāni praṇināya svalīlayā ||
5.44.d:
एवं लब्धवरो व्यासो महेशान्मध्यमेश्वरात् ।
अष्टादश पुराणानि प्रणिनाय स्वलीलया ॥
5.44.m: Having thus received the boon from Maheśa, Madhyameśvara, / Vyāsa composed the eighteen Purāṇas according to his spontaneous play:

5.44.s:
brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā |
bhaviṣyaṃ nāradīyaṃ ca mārkaṇḍeyamataḥ param ||
5.44.d:
ब्राह्मं पाद्मं वैष्णवं च शैवं भागवतं तथा ।
भविष्यं नारदीयं च मार्कण्डेयमतः परम् ॥
5.44.m: The Brāhma, the Pādma, the Vaiṣṇava, the Śaiva, and the Bhāgavata; / the Bhaviṣya, the Nāradīya, and beyond that, the Mārkaṇḍeya;

5.44.s:
āgneyaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ laiṅgaṃ vārāhameva ca |
vāmanākhyaṃ tataḥ kaurmaṃ mātsyaṃ gāruḍameva ca ||
5.44.d:
आग्नेयं ब्रह्मवैवर्तं लैङ्गं वाराहमेव च ।
वामनाख्यं ततः कौर्मं मात्स्यं गारुडमेव च ॥
5.44.m: the Āgneya, the Brahmavaivarta, the Laiṅga, and the Vārāha; / then the one called Vāmana, the Kaurma, the Mātsya, and the Gāruḍa;

5.44.s:
skāndaṃ tathaiva brahmāṇḍākhyaṃ purāṇaṃ ca kīrtitam |
yaśasyaṃ puṇyadaṃ nṝṇāṃ śrotṝṇāṃ śāṅkaraṃ yaśaḥ ||
5.44.d:
स्कान्दं तथैव ब्रह्माण्डाख्यं पुराणं च कीर्तितम् ।
यशस्यं पुण्यदं नॄणां श्रोतॄणां शाङ्करं यशः ॥
5.44.m: the Skānda, and likewise the Purāṇa called Brahmāṇḍa are proclaimed. / The fame of Śaṅkara brings renown and yields merit to men who hear it.

5.44.s:
sūta uvāca |
aṣṭādaśapurāṇānāṃ pūrvaṃ nāmoditaṃ tvayā |
kuru nirvacanaṃ teṣāmidānīṃ vedavittama ||
5.44.d:
सूत उवाच ।
अष्टादशपुराणानां पूर्वं नामोदितं त्वया ।
कुरु निर्वचनं तेषामिदानीं वेदवित्तम ॥
5.44.m: Sūta said: / "Earlier the names of the eighteen Purāṇas were stated by you; / now, O best knower of the Veda, provide their etymological explanations."

5.44.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
ayameva kṛtaḥ praśnastaṇḍinā brahmayoninā |
nandikeśvaramuddiśya sa yadāha bravīmi tat ||
nandikeśvara uvāca |
yatra vaktā svayaṃ taṇḍin brahmā sākṣāccaturmukhaḥ ||
5.44.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
अयमेव कृतः प्रश्नस्तण्डिना ब्रह्मयोनिना ।
नन्दिकेश्वरमुद्दिश्य स यदाह ब्रवीमि तत् ॥
नन्दिकेश्वर उवाच ।
यत्र वक्ता स्वयं तण्डिन् ब्रह्मा साक्षाच्चतुर्मुखः ॥
5.44.m:
Vyāsa said: / "This very question was posed by Taṇḍin, born of Brahmā, / addressed to Nandikeśvara. What he said, that I shall declare:

Nandikeśvara said: / 'That in which the speaker is the four-faced Brahmā himself in visible form, O Taṇḍin,

5.44.s: tasmād brāhmaṃ samākhyātaṃ purāṇaṃ prathamaṃ mune ||
5.44.d: तस्माद् ब्राह्मं समाख्यातं पुराणं प्रथमं मुने ॥
5.44.m: is therefore proclaimed, O sage, as the first Purāṇa, the Brāhma.

5.44.s:
padmakalpasya māhātmyaṃ tatra yasyāmudāhṛtam |
tasmātpādmaṃ samākhyātaṃ purāṇaṃ ca dvitīyakam ||
5.44.d:
पद्मकल्पस्य माहात्म्यं तत्र यस्यामुदाहृतम् ।
तस्मात्पाद्मं समाख्यातं पुराणं च द्वितीयकम् ॥
5.44.m: That in which the eulogy of the Lotus Kalpa is recounted / is on that account proclaimed as the second Purāṇa, the Pādma.

5.44.s:
parāśarakṛtaṃ yattu purāṇaṃ viṣṇubodhakam |
tadeva vyāsakathitaṃ putrapitrorabhedataḥ ||
5.44.d:
पराशरकृतं यत्तु पुराणं विष्णुबोधकम् ।
तदेव व्यासकथितं पुत्रपित्रोरभेदतः ॥
5.44.m: The Purāṇa composed by Parāśara, which makes Viṣṇu known, / that very one is recounted by Vyāsa, because father and son are non-different.

5.44.s:
yatra pūrvottare khaṇḍe śivasya caritaṃ bahu |
śaivametatpurāṇaṃ hi purāṇajñā vadanti ca ||
5.44.d:
यत्र पूर्वोत्तरे खण्डे शिवस्य चरितं बहु ।
शैवमेतत्पुराणं हि पुराणज्ञा वदन्ति च ॥
5.44.m: That in whose first and second parts there are many deeds of Śiva, / this Purāṇa the knowers of the Purāṇas call the Śaiva.

5.44.s:
bhagavatyāśca durgāyāścaritaṃ yatra vidyate |
tattu bhāgavataṃ proktaṃ nanu devīpurāṇakam ||
5.44.d:
भगवत्याश्च दुर्गायाश्चरितं यत्र विद्यते ।
तत्तु भागवतं प्रोक्तं ननु देवीपुराणकम् ॥
5.44.m: And that in which the deed of the goddess Durgā is found, / that is declared to be the Bhāgavata, indeed the Devīpurāṇa.

5.44.s:
nāradoktaṃ purāṇaṃ tu nāradīyaṃ pracakṣate |
yatra vaktābhavattaṇḍin mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ ||
5.44.d:
नारदोक्तं पुराणं तु नारदीयं प्रचक्षते ।
यत्र वक्ताभवत्तण्डिन् मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ॥
5.44.m: The Purāṇa spoken by Nārada they declare to be the Nāradīya. / That in which the speaker was the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya, O Taṇḍin,

5.44.s:
mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇaṃ hi tadākhyātaṃ ca saptamam |
agniyogāttadāgneyaṃ bhaviṣyokterbhaviṣyakam ||
5.44.d:
मार्कण्डेयपुराणं हि तदाख्यातं च सप्तमम् ।
अग्नियोगात्तदाग्नेयं भविष्योक्तेर्भविष्यकम् ॥
5.44.m: is indeed named the Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa, the seventh; / that is the Āgneya from connection with Agni; and the Bhaviṣyaka from the declaration of the future;

5.44.s:
vivartanād brahmaṇastu brahmavaivartamucyate |
liṅgasya caritoktatvātpurāṇaṃ liṅgamucyate ||
5.44.d:
विवर्तनाद् ब्रह्मणस्तु ब्रह्मवैवर्तमुच्यते ।
लिङ्गस्य चरितोक्तत्वात्पुराणं लिङ्गमुच्यते ॥
5.44.m: it is called the Brahmavaivarta because of the evolution of Brahman; / the Purāṇa is called the Laiṅga because the deeds of the liṅga are related;

5.44.s:
varāhasya ca vārāhaṃ purāṇaṃ dvādaśaṃ mune |
yatra skandaḥ svayaṃ śrotā vaktā sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ ||
5.44.d:
वराहस्य च वाराहं पुराणं द्वादशं मुने ।
यत्र स्कन्दः स्वयं श्रोता वक्ता साक्षान्महेश्वरः ॥
5.44.m: and the Vārāha is [the Purāṇa] of the Boar, the twelfth, O sage. / That in which Skanda himself is the hearer and Maheśvara in person is the speaker,

5.44.s:
tattu skāndaṃ samākhyātaṃ vāmanasya tu vāmanam |
kaurmaṃ kūrmasya caritaṃ mātsyaṃ matsyena kīrtitam ||
5.44.d:
तत्तु स्कान्दं समाख्यातं वामनस्य तु वामनम् ।
कौर्मं कूर्मस्य चरितं मात्स्यं मत्स्येन कीर्तितम् ॥
5.44.m: that is proclaimed as the Skānda; that of Vāmana is the Vāmana; / the Kaurma is the deed of the Tortoise; the Mātsya was proclaimed by the Fish;

5.44.s:
garuḍastu svayaṃ vaktā yattad gāruḍasaṃjñakam |
brahmāṇḍacaritoktatvād brahmāṇḍaṃ parikīrtitam ||
5.44.d:
गरुडस्तु स्वयं वक्ता यत्तद् गारुडसंज्ञकम् ।
ब्रह्माण्डचरितोक्तत्वाद् ब्रह्माण्डं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
5.44.m: that in which Garuḍa himself is the speaker is named the Gāruḍa; / it is proclaimed as the Brahmāṇḍa because the deeds of the cosmic egg are narrated.'

5.44.s:
sūta uvāca |
ayameva mayā'kāri praśno vyāsāya dhīmate |
tataḥ sarvapurāṇānāṃ mayā nirvacanaṃ śrutam ||
5.44.d:
सूत उवाच ।
अयमेव मयाऽकारि प्रश्नो व्यासाय धीमते ।
ततः सर्वपुराणानां मया निर्वचनं श्रुतम् ॥
5.44.m: Sūta said: / "This very question was put by me to the wise Vyāsa; / then the explanation of all the Purāṇas was heard by me.

5.44.s:
evaṃ vyāsaḥ samutpannaḥ satyavatyāṃ parāśarāt |
purāṇasaṃhitāścakre mahābhāratamuttamam ||
5.44.d:
एवं व्यासः समुत्पन्नः सत्यवत्यां पराशरात् ।
पुराणसंहिताश्चक्रे महाभारतमुत्तमम् ॥
5.44.m: In this way Vyāsa was born to Satyavatī from Parāśara; / he composed the Purāṇa saṃhitās and the excellent Mahābhārata.

5.44.s:
parāśareṇa saṃyogaḥ punaḥ śantanunā yathā |
satyavatyā iva brahmannaḥ saṃśayitumarhasi ||
5.44.d:
पराशरेण संयोगः पुनः शन्तनुना यथा ।
सत्यवत्या इव ब्रह्मन्नः संशयितुमर्हसि ॥
5.44.m: You ought not to doubt, O brahmin, regarding Satyavatī, / how there was union with Parāśara, and again with Śantanu.

5.44.s:
sakāraṇeyamutpattiḥ kathitāścaryakāriṇī |
mahatāṃ carite caiva guṇā grāhyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
5.44.d:
सकारणेयमुत्पत्तिः कथिताश्चर्यकारिणी ।
महतां चरिते चैव गुणा ग्राह्या विचक्षणैः ॥
5.44.m: This wondrous birth has been related with its cause; / and in the conduct of the great, the wise should take only the virtues.

5.44.s:
idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti paṭhatyapi |
sa sarvapāpanirmukta ṛṣiloke mahīyate ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.44.d:
इदं रहस्यं परमं यः शृणोति पठत्यपि ।
स सर्वपापनिर्मुक्त ऋषिलोके महीयते ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.44.m:
Whoever hears or even reads this supreme secret / is freed from all sins and honored in the world of the sages."

Salutation to holy Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.45.s:
munaya ūcuḥ |
śrutā śambhoḥ kathā ramyā nānākhyānasamanvitā |
nānāvatārasaṃyuktā bhuktimuktipradā nṛṇām ||
5.45.d:
मुनय ऊचुः ।
श्रुता शम्भोः कथा रम्या नानाख्यानसमन्विता ।
नानावतारसंयुक्ता भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदा नृणाम् ॥
5.45.m: The sages said: / "The charming narrative of Śambhu has been heard, accompanied by various stories, / endowed with his various incarnations, granting enjoyment and liberation to men.

5.45.s:
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmastvatto brahmavidāṃvara |
caritraṃ jagadambāyā bhagavatyā manoharam ||
5.45.d:
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामस्त्वत्तो ब्रह्मविदांवर ।
चरित्रं जगदम्बाया भगवत्या मनोहरम् ॥
5.45.m: Now we wish to hear from you, O best among the knowers of Brahman, / the captivating deeds of the goddess, the Mother of the world,

5.45.s:
parabrahmamaheśasya śaktirādyā sanātanī |
umā yā samabhikhyātā trailokyajananī parā ||
5.45.d:
परब्रह्ममहेशस्य शक्तिराद्या सनातनी ।
उमा या समभिख्याता त्रैलोक्यजननी परा ॥
5.45.m: the primordial, eternal Śakti of the supreme Brahman Maheśa, / who is celebrated as Umā, the supreme Mother of the three worlds.

5.45.s:
satī haimavatī tasyā avatāradvayaṃ śrutam |
aparānavatārāṃstvaṃ brūhi sūta mahāmate ||
5.45.d:
सती हैमवती तस्या अवतारद्वयं श्रुतम् ।
अपरानवतारांस्त्वं ब्रूहि सूत महामते ॥
5.45.m: Her two incarnations as Satī and Haimavatī have been heard. / Tell of her other incarnations, O high-minded Sūta.

5.45.s:
ko virajyeta matimān guṇaśravaṇakarmaṇi |
śrīmāturjñānino yāni na tyajanti kadācana ||
5.45.d:
को विरज्येत मतिमान् गुणश्रवणकर्मणि ।
श्रीमातुर्ज्ञानिनो यानि न त्यजन्ति कदाचन ॥
5.45.m: What wise man would lose interest in the act of hearing the virtues / of the glorious Mother, which the wise never abandon?"

5.45.s:
sūta uvāca |
dhanyā yūyaṃ mahātmānaḥ kṛtakṛtyāḥ stha sarvadā |
yatpṛcchatha parāmbāyā umāyāścaritaṃ mahat ||
5.45.d:
सूत उवाच ।
धन्या यूयं महात्मानः कृतकृत्याः स्थ सर्वदा ।
यत्पृच्छथ पराम्बाया उमायाश्चरितं महत् ॥
5.45.m: Sūta said: / "Fortunate are you, great-souled ones; you are ever accomplished in your aims, / since you ask about the great deeds of the supreme Mother, Umā.

5.45.s:
śṛṇvatāṃ pṛcchatāṃ caiva tathā vācayatāṃ ca tat |
pādāmbujarajāṃsyeva tīrthāni munayo viduḥ ||
5.45.d:
शृण्वतां पृच्छतां चैव तथा वाचयतां च तत् ।
पादाम्बुजरजांस्येव तीर्थानि मुनयो विदुः ॥
5.45.m: Sages consider the very dust of the lotus feet of those who listen to it, ask about it, and recite it / to be sacred bathing places.

5.45.s:
te dhanyā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syurdhanyā teṣāṃ prasūḥ kulam |
yeṣāṃ cittaṃ bhavellīnaṃ śrīdevyāṃ parasaṃvidi ||
5.45.d:
ते धन्या कृतकृत्याः स्युर्धन्या तेषां प्रसूः कुलम् ।
येषां चित्तं भवेल्लीनं श्रीदेव्यां परसंविदि ॥
5.45.m: Fortunate are they, their purpose achieved, fortunate their mother and lineage, / whose minds are absorbed in the glorious Goddess, the Supreme Consciousness.

5.45.s:
ye na stuvanti deveśīṃ sarvakāraṇakāraṇām |
māyāguṇairmohitāḥ syurhatabhāgyā na saṃśayaḥ ||
5.45.d:
ये न स्तुवन्ति देवेशीं सर्वकारणकारणाम् ।
मायागुणैर्मोहिताः स्युर्हतभाग्या न संशयः ॥
5.45.m: Those who do not praise the Ruler of Gods, the Cause of all causes, / are deluded by the strands of māyā and ill-fated, beyond doubt.

5.45.s:
na bhajanti mahādevīṃ karuṇārasasāgarām |
andhakūpe patantyete ghore saṃsārarūpiṇi ||
5.45.d:
न भजन्ति महादेवीं करुणारससागराम् ।
अन्धकूपे पतन्त्येते घोरे संसाररूपिणि ॥
5.45.m: Those who do not worship the Great Goddess, the ocean of the essence of compassion, / plunge into the blind well in the form of this terrible worldly existence.

5.45.s:
gaṅgāṃ vihāya tṛptyarthaṃ maruvāri yathā vrajet |
vihāya devīṃ tadbhinnaṃ tathā devāntaraṃ vrajet ||
5.45.d:
गङ्गां विहाय तृप्त्यर्थं मरुवारि यथा व्रजेत् ।
विहाय देवीं तद्भिन्नं तथा देवान्तरं व्रजेत् ॥
5.45.m: Just as one might leave the Gaṅgā and go to desert water to quench one's thirst, / so would one leave the Goddess and go to another deity distinct from Her.

5.45.s:
yasyāḥ smaraṇamātreṇa puruṣārthacatuṣṭayam |
anāyāsena labhate kastyajettāṃ narottamaḥ ||
5.45.d:
यस्याः स्मरणमात्रेण पुरुषार्थचतुष्टयम् ।
अनायासेन लभते कस्त्यजेत्तां नरोत्तमः ॥
5.45.m: By the mere remembrance of whom one effortlessly attains / the four aims of life—what best among men would abandon Her?

5.45.s:
etatpṛṣṭaḥ purā medhāḥ surathena mahātmanā |
yaduktaṃ medhasā pūrvaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva vadāmi te ||
5.45.d:
एतत्पृष्टः पुरा मेधाः सुरथेन महात्मना ।
यदुक्तं मेधसा पूर्वं तच्छृणुष्व वदामि ते ॥
5.45.m: Concerning this, the sage Medhas was asked in ancient times by the noble Suratha. / What was previously spoken by Medhas—listen to that, I shall tell you.

5.45.s:
svārociṣe'ntare pūrvaṃ viratho nāma pārthivaḥ |
surathastasya putro'bhūnmahābalaparākramaḥ ||
5.45.d:
स्वारोचिषेऽन्तरे पूर्वं विरथो नाम पार्थिवः ।
सुरथस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभून्महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
5.45.m: Formerly, in the Svārociṣa Manvantara, there was an earthly king named Viratha; / his son was Suratha, endowed with great strength and prowess.

5.45.s:
dānaśauṇḍaḥ satyavādī svadharmakuśalaḥ kṛtī |
devībhakto dayāsindhuḥ prajānāṃ paripālakaḥ ||
5.45.d:
दानशौण्डः सत्यवादी स्वधर्मकुशलः कृती ।
देवीभक्तो दयासिन्धुः प्रजानां परिपालकः ॥
5.45.m: Generous in giving, truthful in speech, skilled in his own duty, accomplished, / devoted to the Goddess, an ocean of compassion, a protector of his subjects.

5.45.s:
pṛthivīṃ śāsatastasya pākaśāsanatejasaḥ |
babhūvurnava ye bhūpāḥ pṛthvīgrahaṇatatparāḥ ||
5.45.d:
पृथिवीं शासतस्तस्य पाकशासनतेजसः ।
बभूवुर्नव ये भूपाः पृथ्वीग्रहणतत्पराः ॥
5.45.m: As he ruled the earth, possessing the splendour of Indra, / there arose nine kings bent upon seizing his land.

5.45.s:
kolānāmnīṃ rājadhānīṃ rurudhustasya bhūpateḥ |
taiḥ samaṃ tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ samapadyata dāruṇam ||
5.45.d:
कोलानाम्नीं राजधानीं रुरुधुस्तस्य भूपतेः ।
तैः समं तुमुलं युद्धं समपद्यत दारुणम् ॥
5.45.m: They besieged the capital of that king, named Kolā; / a fierce and terrible battle took place between them.

5.45.s:
yuddhe sa nirjito bhūpaḥ prabalaistairdviṣadgaṇaiḥ |
ujjāsitaśca kolāyā hṛtvā rājyamaśeṣataḥ ||
5.45.d:
युद्धे स निर्जितो भूपः प्रबलैस्तैर्द्विषद्गणैः ।
उज्जासितश्च कोलाया हृत्वा राज्यमशेषतः ॥
5.45.m: Defeated in battle by those mighty hosts of enemies / and having his kingdom completely seized, he was driven out of Kolā.

5.45.s:
sa rājā svapurīmetyākarodrājyaṃ svamantribhiḥ |
tatrāpi ca mahāpakṣairvipakṣaiḥ sa parājitaḥ ||
5.45.d:
स राजा स्वपुरीमेत्याकरोद्राज्यं स्वमन्त्रिभिः ।
तत्रापि च महापक्षैर्विपक्षैः स पराजितः ॥
5.45.m: That king returned to his own city and ruled with his ministers; / even there, he was defeated by powerful adversaries.

5.45.s:
daivācchatrutvamāpannairamātyapramukhairgaṇaiḥ |
kośasthitaṃ ca yadvittaṃ tatsarvaṃ cātmasātkṛtam ||
5.45.d:
दैवाच्छत्रुत्वमापन्नैरमात्यप्रमुखैर्गणैः ।
कोशस्थितं च यद्वित्तं तत्सर्वं चात्मसात्कृतम् ॥
5.45.m: By the factions headed by ministers who had become enemies through fate, / all the treasure kept in the treasury was appropriated for themselves.

5.45.s:
tataḥ sa nirgato rājā nagarānmṛgayāchalāt |
asahāyo'śvamāruhya jagāma gahanaṃ vanam ||
5.45.d:
ततः स निर्गतो राजा नगरान्मृगयाछलात् ।
असहायोऽश्वमारुह्य जगाम गहनं वनम् ॥
5.45.m: Then that king departed from the city on the pretext of hunting; / alone, having mounted a horse, he went into the dense forest.

5.45.s:
itastatastatra gacchanrājā munivarāśramam |
dadarśa kusumārāmabhrājitaṃ sarvatodiśam ||
5.45.d:
इतस्ततस्तत्र गच्छन्राजा मुनिवराश्रमम् ।
ददर्श कुसुमारामभ्राजितं सर्वतोदिशम् ॥
5.45.m: Wandering here and there, the king saw the hermitage of an excellent sage, / radiant on every side with gardens of blossoms,

5.45.s:
vedadhvanisamākīrṇaṃ śāntajantusamāśritam |
śiṣyaiḥ praśiṣyaistacchiṣyaiḥ samantātpariveṣṭitam ||
5.45.d:
वेदध्वनिसमाकीर्णं शान्तजन्तुसमाश्रितम् ।
शिष्यैः प्रशिष्यैस्तच्छिष्यैः समन्तात्परिवेष्टितम् ॥
5.45.m: filled with the sound of the Vedas, resorted to by tranquil animals, / surrounded on all sides by disciples, disciples of disciples, and their students.

5.45.s:
vyāghrādayo mahāvīryā alpavīryānmahāmate |
tadāśrame na bādhante dvijavaryaprabhāvataḥ ||
5.45.d:
व्याघ्रादयो महावीर्या अल्पवीर्यान्महामते ।
तदाश्रमे न बाधन्ते द्विजवर्यप्रभावतः ॥
5.45.m: Tigers and other animals of great prowess, O wise one, / did not harass weaker creatures in that hermitage, by the power of the foremost of the twice-born.

5.45.s:
uvāsa tatra nṛpatirmahākāruṇiko budhaḥ |
satkṛto munināthena suvaco bhojanāsanaiḥ ||
5.45.d:
उवास तत्र नृपतिर्महाकारुणिको बुधः ।
सत्कृतो मुनिनाथेन सुवचो भोजनासनैः ॥
5.45.m: The king, deeply compassionate and wise, dwelt there, / honoured by the lord of sages with kind words, food, and a seat.

5.45.s:
ekadā sa mahārājaścintāmāpa duratyayām |
aho me hīnabhāgyasya durbuddherhīnatejasaḥ ||
5.45.d:
एकदा स महाराजश्चिन्तामाप दुरत्ययाम् ।
अहो मे हीनभाग्यस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्हीनतेजसः ॥
5.45.m: Once that great king was seized with insurmountable worry: / 'Alas for me, unfortunate, foolish, and bereft of splendour!

5.45.s:
hṛtaṃ rājyamaśeṣeṇa śatruvargairmadoddhataiḥ |
matpūrvai rakṣitaṃ rājyaṃ śatrubhirbhujyate'dhunā ||
5.45.d:
हृतं राज्यमशेषेण शत्रुवर्गैर्मदोद्धतैः ।
मत्पूर्वै रक्षितं राज्यं शत्रुभिर्भुज्यतेऽधुना ॥
5.45.m: My kingdom has been wholly seized by hordes of enemies insolent with pride; / the kingdom protected by my ancestors is now enjoyed by enemies.

5.45.s:
mādṛśaścaitravaṃśe'sminna ko'pyāsīnmahīpatiḥ |
kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ rājyaṃ labheya hi ||
5.45.d:
मादृशश्चैत्रवंशेऽस्मिन्न कोऽप्यासीन्महीपतिः ।
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि कथं राज्यं लभेय हि ॥
5.45.m: In this dynasty of Caitra there has never been any king like me. / What shall I do? Where shall I go? How indeed might I regain my kingdom?

5.45.s:
amātyā mantriṇaścaiva māmakā ye sanātanāḥ |
na jāne kaṃ ca nṛpatiṃ samāsādyādhunāsate ||
5.45.d:
अमात्या मन्त्रिणश्चैव मामका ये सनातनाः ।
न जाने कं च नृपतिं समासाद्याधुनासते ॥
5.45.m: My traditional ministers and counsellors— / I do not know which king they have now approached and serve.

5.45.s:
vināśya rājyamadhunā na jāne kāṃ gatiṃ gatāḥ |
raṇabhūmimahotsāhā arivarganikartanāḥ ||
5.45.d:
विनाश्य राज्यमधुना न जाने कां गतिं गताः ।
रणभूमिमहोत्साहा अरिवर्गनिकर्तनाः ॥
5.45.m: Now that the kingdom is destroyed, I do not know what state they have reached— / they who had great zeal on the battlefield, cutters-down of enemy hosts.

5.45.s:
māmakā ye mahāśūrā nṛpamanyaṃ bhajanti te |
parvatābhā gajā aśvā vātavadvegagāminaḥ ||
5.45.d:
मामका ये महाशूरा नृपमन्यं भजन्ति ते ।
पर्वताभा गजा अश्वा वातवद्वेगगामिनः ॥
5.45.m: My great heroes—are they serving another king? / And the mountain-like elephants, the horses swift as the wind—

5.45.s:
pūrvapūrvārjitaḥ kośaḥ pālyate tairna vādhunā |
evaṃ mohavaśaṃ yāto rājā paramadhārmikaḥ ||
5.45.d:
पूर्वपूर्वार्जितः कोशः पाल्यते तैर्न वाधुना ।
एवं मोहवशं यातो राजा परमधार्मिकः ॥
5.45.m: is the treasury accumulated by my predecessors being preserved by them now, or not?' / Thus fell into the sway of delusion that king of supreme righteousness.

5.45.s:
etasminnantare tatra vaiśyaḥ kaścitsamāgataḥ |
rājā papraccha kastvaṃ bhoḥ kimarthamiha cāgataḥ ||
5.45.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र वैश्यः कश्चित्समागतः ।
राजा पप्रच्छ कस्त्वं भोः किमर्थमिह चागतः ॥
5.45.m: At that moment, a certain merchant arrived there. / The king asked: 'Who are you, sir? And for what purpose have you come here?

5.45.s:
durmanā lakṣyase kasmādetanme brūhi sāmpratam |
ityākarṇya vaco ramyaṃ narapālena bhāṣitam ||
5.45.d:
दुर्मना लक्ष्यसे कस्मादेतन्मे ब्रूहि साम्प्रतम् ।
इत्याकर्ण्य वचो रम्यं नरपालेन भाषितम् ॥
5.45.m: Why do you appear dejected? Tell me this now.' / Hearing these pleasant words spoken by the protector of men,

5.45.s:
dṛgbhyāṃ vimuñcannaśrūṇi samādhirvaiśyapuṅgavaḥ |
pratyuvāca mahīpālaṃ praṇayāvanatāṃ giram ||
5.45.d:
दृग्भ्यां विमुञ्चन्नश्रूणि समाधिर्वैश्यपुङ्गवः ।
प्रत्युवाच महीपालं प्रणयावनतां गिरम् ॥
5.45.m: shedding tears from both eyes, Samādhi, the foremost of merchants, / replied to the earth-ruler in words lowered with affection.

5.45.s:
vaiśya uvāca |
samādhirnāma vaiśyo'haṃ dhanivaṃśasamudbhavaḥ |
putradārādibhistyakto dhanalobhānmahīpate ||
5.45.d:
वैश्य उवाच ।
समाधिर्नाम वैश्योऽहं धनिवंशसमुद्भवः ।
पुत्रदारादिभिस्त्यक्तो धनलोभान्महीपते ॥
5.45.m: The merchant said: / 'I am a merchant named Samādhi, born into a wealthy family; / I have been cast out by my sons, wife, and others through greed for wealth, O ruler of the earth.

5.45.s:
vanamabhyāgato rājanduḥkhitaḥ svena karmaṇā |
so'haṃ putraprapautrāṇāṃ kalatrāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ||
5.45.d:
वनमभ्यागतो राजन्दुःखितः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
सोऽहं पुत्रप्रपौत्राणां कलत्राणां तथैव च ॥
5.45.m: I have come to the forest, O King, aggrieved by my own past action. / Even so, concerning my sons, great-grandsons, and wives,

5.45.s:
bhrātṛṇāṃ bhrātṛputrāṇāṃ pareṣāṃ suhṛdāṃ tathā |
na vedmi kuśalaṃ samyak karuṇāsāgara prabho ||
5.45.d:
भ्रातृणां भ्रातृपुत्राणां परेषां सुहृदां तथा ।
न वेद्मि कुशलं सम्यक् करुणासागर प्रभो ॥
5.45.m: and my brothers, nephews, others, and friends, / I do not know properly of their welfare, O lord, ocean of compassion.'

5.45.s:
rājovāca |
niṣkāsito yaiḥ putrādyairdurvṛttairdhanagardhibhiḥ |
teṣu kiṃ bhavatā prītiḥ kriyate mūrkhajantuvat ||
5.45.d:
राजोवाच ।
निष्कासितो यैः पुत्राद्यैर्दुर्वृत्तैर्धनगर्धिभिः ।
तेषु किं भवता प्रीतिः क्रियते मूर्खजन्तुवत् ॥
5.45.m: The king said: / 'By the sons and others, wicked and covetous of wealth, by whom you have been expelled— / why do you show affection toward them like a foolish creature?'

5.45.s:
vaiśya uvāca |
samyaguktaṃ tvayā rājanvacaḥ sārārthabṛṃhitam |
tathāpi snehapāśena mohyate'tīva me manaḥ ||
5.45.d:
वैश्य उवाच ।
सम्यगुक्तं त्वया राजन्वचः सारार्थबृंहितम् ।
तथापि स्नेहपाशेन मोह्यतेऽतीव मे मनः ॥
5.45.m: The merchant said: / 'You have spoken well, O King, words fortified with meaningful truth; / even so, my mind is exceedingly deluded by the bond of affection.

5.45.s:
evaṃ mohākulau vaiśyapārthivau munisattama |
jagmaturmunivaryasya medhasaḥ sannidhiṃ tadā ||
5.45.d:
एवं मोहाकुलौ वैश्यपार्थिवौ मुनिसत्तम ।
जग्मतुर्मुनिवर्यस्य मेधसः सन्निधिं तदा ॥
5.45.m: Thus troubled by delusion, O best of sages, the merchant and the king / then went into the presence of the excellent sage Medhas.

5.45.s:
sa vaiśyarājasahito nararājaḥ pratāpavān |
praṇanāma mahāvīraḥ śirasā yogināṃ varam ||
5.45.d:
स वैश्यराजसहितो नरराजः प्रतापवान् ।
प्रणनाम महावीरः शिरसा योगिनां वरम् ॥
5.45.m: That mighty warrior, the glorious king of men, together with the merchant, / bowed his head before the best of yogins.

5.45.s:
baddhvāñjalimimāṃ vācamuvāca nṛpatirmunim |
bhagavannāvayormohaṃ chettumarhasi sāmpratam ||
5.45.d:
बद्ध्वाञ्जलिमिमां वाचमुवाच नृपतिर्मुनिम् ।
भगवन्नावयोर्मोहं छेत्तुमर्हसि साम्प्रतम् ॥
5.45.m: Folding his hands in reverence, the king spoke this word to the sage: / 'O venerable one, you ought now to sever the delusion of us both.

5.45.s:
ahaṃ rājaśriyā tyakto gahanaṃ vanamāśritaḥ |
tathāpi hṛtarājyasya toṣo naivābhijāyate ||
5.45.d:
अहं राजश्रिया त्यक्तो गहनं वनमाश्रितः ।
तथापि हृतराज्यस्य तोषो नैवाभिजायते ॥
5.45.m: Abandoned by royal fortune, I have resorted to the dense forest; / even so, bereft of my kingdom, contentment does not arise in me.

5.45.s:
ayaṃ ca vaiśyaḥ svajanairdārādyairniṣkṛto gṛhāt |
tathāpyetasya mamatā na nivṛttiṃ samaśnute ||
5.45.d:
अयं च वैश्यः स्वजनैर्दाराद्यैर्निष्कृतो गृहात् ।
तथाप्येतस्य ममता न निवृत्तिं समश्नुते ॥
5.45.m: And this merchant has been expelled from home by his own kin, wife, and others; / yet his sense of possessiveness attains no cessation.

5.45.s:
kimatra kāraṇaṃ brūhi jñāninorapi no manaḥ |
mohena vyākulaṃ jātaṃ mahatyeṣā hi mūrkhatā ||
5.45.d:
किमत्र कारणं ब्रूहि ज्ञानिनोरपि नो मनः ।
मोहेन व्याकुलं जातं महत्येषा हि मूर्खता ॥
5.45.m: Tell me what the cause of this is: even though the two of us possess knowledge, our minds / have become confounded by delusion; this is indeed a great folly.'

5.45.s:
ṛṣiruvāca |
mahāmāyā jagaddhātrī śaktirūpā sanātanī |
sā mohayati sarveṣāṃ samākṛṣya manāṃsi vai ||
5.45.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
महामाया जगद्धात्री शक्तिरूपा सनातनी ।
सा मोहयति सर्वेषां समाकृष्य मनांसि वै ॥
5.45.m: The sage said: / 'Mahāmāyā, the bearer of the universe, whose form is the eternal Śakti— / She indeed deludes the minds of all, having drawn them in.

5.45.s:
brahmādayaḥ surāḥ sarve yanmāyāmohitāḥ prabho |
na jānanti paraṃ tattvaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca kā kathā ||
5.45.d:
ब्रह्मादयः सुराः सर्वे यन्मायामोहिताः प्रभो ।
न जानन्ति परं तत्त्वं मनुष्याणां च का कथा ॥
5.45.m: All the gods, Brahmā and the rest, deluded by Her Māyā, O lord, / do not know the supreme reality; what then to say of human beings?

5.45.s:
sā sṛjatyakhilaṃ viśvaṃ saiva pālayatīti ca |
saiva saṃharate kāle triguṇā parameśvarī ||
5.45.d:
सा सृजत्यखिलं विश्वं सैव पालयतीति च ।
सैव संहरते काले त्रिगुणा परमेश्वरी ॥
5.45.m: She creates the entire universe, and She alone preserves it; / She alone dissolves it in time—the supreme Sovereign composed of the three guṇas.

5.45.s:
yasyopari prasannā sā varadā kāmarūpiṇī |
sa eva mohamatyeti nānyathā nṛpasattama ||
5.45.d:
यस्योपरि प्रसन्ना सा वरदा कामरूपिणी ।
स एव मोहमत्येति नान्यथा नृपसत्तम ॥
5.45.m: He upon whom She, the granter of boons who can assume any form at will, is pleased / is the one who overcomes delusion, not otherwise, O best of kings.'

5.45.s:
rājovāca |
kā sā devī mahāmāyā yā ca mohayate'khilān |
kathaṃ jātā ca sā devī kṛpayā vada me mune ||
5.45.d:
राजोवाच ।
का सा देवी महामाया या च मोहयतेऽखिलान् ।
कथं जाता च सा देवी कृपया वद मे मुने ॥
5.45.m: The king said: / 'Who is that Goddess Mahāmāyā who deludes all? / And how was that Goddess born? Please tell me, O sage.'

5.45.s:
ṛṣiruvāca |
jagatyekārṇave jāte śeṣamāstīrya yogarāṭ |
yoganidrāmupāśritya yadā suṣvāpa keśavaḥ ||
5.45.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
जगत्येकार्णवे जाते शेषमास्तीर्य योगराट् ।
योगनिद्रामुपाश्रित्य यदा सुष्वाप केशवः ॥
5.45.m: The sage said: / 'When the universe had become a single cosmic ocean, having spread out Śeṣa, the king of yogins, / Keśava, fell asleep, resorting to yogic sleep.

5.45.s:
tadā dvāvasurau jātau viṣṇoḥ karṇamalena vai |
madhukaiṭabhanāmānau vikhyātau pṛthivītale ||
5.45.d:
तदा द्वावसुरौ जातौ विष्णोः कर्णमलेन वै ।
मधुकैटभनामानौ विख्यातौ पृथिवीतले ॥
5.45.m: Then two asuras were born from the ear-wax of Viṣṇu, / famous throughout the earth by the names Madhu and Kaiṭabha,

5.45.s:
pralayārkaprabhau ghorau mahākāyau mahāhanū |
daṃṣṭrākarālavadanau bhakṣayantau jaganti vā ||
5.45.d:
प्रलयार्कप्रभौ घोरौ महाकायौ महाहनू ।
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनौ भक्षयन्तौ जगन्ति वा ॥
5.45.m: having the brilliance of the sun of cosmic dissolution, terrible, with huge bodies and huge jaws, / their faces frightful with fangs, as if devouring the worlds.

5.45.s:
tau dṛṣṭvā bhagavannābhipaṅkaje kamalāsanam |
hananāyodyatāvāstāṃ kastvaṃ bhoriti vādinau ||
5.45.d:
तौ दृष्ट्वा भगवन्नाभिपङ्कजे कमलासनम् ।
हननायोद्यतावास्तां कस्त्वं भोरिति वादिनौ ॥
5.45.m: Seeing the lotus-seated [Brahmā] on the lotus of the Lord’s navel, / those two prepared to kill him, saying: 'Who are you, sir?'

5.45.s:
samālokya tu tau daityau surajyeṣṭho janārdanam |
śayānaṃ ca payombhodhau tuṣṭāva parameśvarīm ||
5.45.d:
समालोक्य तु तौ दैत्यौ सुरज्येष्ठो जनार्दनम् ।
शयानं च पयोम्भोधौ तुष्टाव परमेश्वरीम् ॥
5.45.m: Beholding those two Daityas, the eldest of the gods, [seeing] Janārdana / asleep in the ocean of milk, praised the supreme Sovereign.

5.45.s:
brahmovāca |
rakṣa rakṣa mahāmāye śaraṇāgatavatsale |
etābhyāṃ ghorarūpābhyāṃ daityābhyāṃ jagadambike ||
5.45.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
रक्ष रक्ष महामाये शरणागतवत्सले ।
एताभ्यां घोररूपाभ्यां दैत्याभ्यां जगदम्बिके ॥
5.45.m: Brahmā said: / 'Protect, protect [me], O Mahāmāyā, affectionate toward those who seek refuge! / From these two demons of terrible form, O Mother of the universe!

5.45.s:
praṇamāmi mahāmāyāṃ yoganidrāmumāṃ satīm |
kālarātriṃ mahārātriṃ moharātriṃ parātparām ||
5.45.d:
प्रणमामि महामायां योगनिद्रामुमां सतीम् ।
कालरात्रिं महारात्रिं मोहरात्रिं परात्पराम् ॥
5.45.m: I bow to Mahāmāyā, Yoganidrā, Umā, Satī, / Kālarātri, Mahārātri, Moharātri, higher than the highest,

5.45.s:
tridevajananīṃ nityāṃ bhaktābhīṣṭaphalapradām |
pālinīṃ sarvadevānāṃ karuṇāvaruṇālayām ||
5.45.d:
त्रिदेवजननीं नित्यां भक्ताभीष्टफलप्रदाम् ।
पालिनीं सर्वदेवानां करुणावरुणालयाम् ॥
5.45.m: the eternal Mother of the three gods, granter of the desired fruit to devotees, / protector of all the gods, ocean of compassion!

5.45.s:
tvatprabhāvādahaṃ brahmā mādhavo girijāpatiḥ |
sṛjatyavati saṃsāraṃ kāle saṃharatīti ca ||
5.45.d:
त्वत्प्रभावादहं ब्रह्मा माधवो गिरिजापतिः ।
सृजत्यवति संसारं काले संहरतीति च ॥
5.45.m: By your power I, Brahmā, create, Mādhava preserves the world, / and the husband of Girijā destroys it at the end of time.

5.45.s:
tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hrīstvaṃ buddhirvimalā matā |
tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭistvamevāmba śāntiḥ kṣāntiḥ kṣudhā dayā ||
5.45.d:
त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा त्वं ह्रीस्त्वं बुद्धिर्विमला मता ।
तुष्टिः पुष्टिस्त्वमेवाम्ब शान्तिः क्षान्तिः क्षुधा दया ॥
5.45.m: You are svāhā, you are svadhā, you are hrī, you are regarded as pure intellect; / you alone are contentment, nourishment, O Mother, peace, forbearance, hunger, and compassion.

5.45.s:
viṣṇumāyā tvamevāmba tvameva cetanā matā |
tvaṃ śaktiḥ paramā proktā lajjā tṛṣṇā tvameva ca ||
5.45.d:
विष्णुमाया त्वमेवाम्ब त्वमेव चेतना मता ।
त्वं शक्तिः परमा प्रोक्ता लज्जा तृष्णा त्वमेव च ॥
5.45.m: You alone are the māyā of Viṣṇu, O Mother, you are considered consciousness; / you are declared the supreme śakti, and you alone are modesty and craving.

5.45.s:
bhrāntistvaṃ smṛtirūpā tvaṃ mātṛrūpeṇa saṃsthitā |
tvaṃ lakṣmīrbhavane puṃsāṃ puṇyācārapravartinām ||
5.45.d:
भ्रान्तिस्त्वं स्मृतिरूपा त्वं मातृरूपेण संस्थिता ।
त्वं लक्ष्मीर्भवने पुंसां पुण्याचारप्रवर्तिनाम् ॥
5.45.m: You are delusion, you have the form of memory, you reside in the form of a mother; / you are Lakṣmī in the house of men devoted to virtuous conduct.

5.45.s:
tvaṃ jātistvaṃ matā vṛttirvyāptirūpā tvameva hi |
tvameva cittirūpeṇa vyāpya kṛtsnaṃ pratiṣṭhitā ||
5.45.d:
त्वं जातिस्त्वं मता वृत्तिर्व्याप्तिरूपा त्वमेव हि ।
त्वमेव चित्तिरूपेण व्याप्य कृत्स्नं प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
5.45.m: You are generic form, you are regarded as function, you indeed have the form of pervasion; / you alone, having pervaded everything in the form of consciousness, stand established.

5.45.s:
sā tvametau durādharṣāvasurau mohayāmbike |
prabodhaya jagadyone nārāyaṇamajaṃ vibhum ||
5.45.d:
सा त्वमेतौ दुराधर्षावसुरौ मोहयाम्बिके ।
प्रबोधय जगद्योने नारायणमजं विभुम् ॥
5.45.m: Delude these two invincible asuras, O Ambikā! / Awaken the unborn, all-pervading Nārāyaṇa, the origin of the universe!'

5.45.s:
ṛṣiruvāca |
brahmaṇā prārthitā seyaṃ madhukaiṭabhanāśane |
mahāvidyā jagaddhātrī sarvavidyādhidevatā ||
5.45.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
ब्रह्मणा प्रार्थिता सेयं मधुकैटभनाशने ।
महाविद्या जगद्धात्री सर्वविद्याधिदेवता ॥
5.45.m: The sage said: / Entreated thus by Brahmā for the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, / that Mahāvidyā, the upholder of the universe, the presiding deity of all vidyās,

5.45.s:
dvādaśyāṃ phālgunasyaiva śuklāyāṃ samabhūnnṛpa |
mahākālīti vikhyātā śaktistrailokyamohinī ||
5.45.d:
द्वादश्यां फाल्गुनस्यैव शुक्लायां समभून्नृप ।
महाकालीति विख्याता शक्तिस्त्रैलोक्यमोहिनी ॥
5.45.m: manifested on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, O king, / renowned as Mahākālī, the śakti that deludes the three worlds.

5.45.s:
tato'bhavadviyadvāṇī mā bhaiṣīḥ kamalāsana |
kaṇṭakaṃ nāśayāmyadya hatvājau madhukaiṭabhau ||
5.45.d:
ततोऽभवद्वियद्वाणी मा भैषीः कमलासन ।
कण्टकं नाशयाम्यद्य हत्वाजौ मधुकैटभौ ॥
5.45.m: Then came a voice from the sky: 'Do not fear, lotus-seated [Brahmā]! / Having slain Madhu and Kaiṭabha in battle, I shall destroy the thorn today.'

5.45.s:
ityuktvā sā mahāmāyā netravaktrādito hareḥ |
nirgamya darśane tasthau brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ ||
5.45.d:
इत्युक्त्वा सा महामाया नेत्रवक्त्रादितो हरेः ।
निर्गम्य दर्शने तस्थौ ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ॥
5.45.m: Having said this, that Mahāmāyā, issuing from the eyes, mouth, and other parts of Hari, / stood in the sight of Brahmā, who was born of the unmanifest.

5.45.s:
uttasthau ca hṛṣīkeśo devadevo janārdanaḥ |
sa dadarśa puro daityau madhukaiṭabhasaṃjñakau ||
5.45.d:
उत्तस्थौ च हृषीकेशो देवदेवो जनार्दनः ।
स ददर्श पुरो दैत्यौ मधुकैटभसंज्ञकौ ॥
5.45.m: And Hṛṣīkeśa, the god of gods, Janārdana, arose. / He saw before him the two daityas named Madhu and Kaiṭabha.

5.45.s:
tābhyāṃ pravavṛtte yuddhaṃ viṣṇoratulatejasaḥ |
pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi bāhuyuddhamabhūttadā ||
5.45.d:
ताभ्यां प्रववृत्ते युद्धं विष्णोरतुलतेजसः ।
पञ्चवर्षसहस्राणि बाहुयुद्धमभूत्तदा ॥
5.45.m: A battle ensued between them and Viṣṇu of peerless splendor; / five thousand years of hand-to-hand combat then took place.

5.45.s:
mahāmāyāprabhāveṇa mohitau dānavottamau |
jajalpatū ramākāntaṃ gṛhāṇa varamīpsitam ||
5.45.d:
महामायाप्रभावेण मोहितौ दानवोत्तमौ ।
जजल्पतू रमाकान्तं गृहाण वरमीप्सितम् ॥
5.45.m: Deluded by the power of Mahāmāyā, the two foremost dānavas / said to the beloved of Ramā: 'Receive a boon of your choice!'

5.45.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca |
mayi prasannau yadi vāṃ dīyatāmeṣa me varaḥ |
mama vadhyāvubhau nānyaṃ yuvābhyāṃ prārthaye varam ||
5.45.d:
नारायण उवाच ।
मयि प्रसन्नौ यदि वां दीयतामेष मे वरः ।
मम वध्यावुभौ नान्यं युवाभ्यां प्रार्थये वरम् ॥
5.45.m: Nārāyaṇa said: / 'If you two are pleased with me, let this boon be granted to me: / that you both be slain by me; no other boon do I ask of you two.'

5.45.s:
ṛṣiruvāca |
ekārṇavāṃ mahīṃ dṛṣṭvā procatuḥ keśavaṃ vacaḥ |
āvāṃ jahi na yatrāsau dharaṇī payasāplutā ||
5.45.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
एकार्णवां महीं दृष्ट्वा प्रोचतुः केशवं वचः ।
आवां जहि न यत्रासौ धरणी पयसाप्लुता ॥
5.45.m: The sage said: / Seeing the earth merged into a single ocean, the two said this word to Keśava: / 'Slay us where this earth is not submerged in water.'

5.45.s:
tathāstu procya bhagavāṃścakramutthāpya sūjjvalam |
ciccheda śirasī kṛtvā svakīyajaghane tayoḥ ||
5.45.d:
तथास्तु प्रोच्य भगवांश्चक्रमुत्थाप्य सूज्ज्वलम् ।
चिच्छेद शिरसी कृत्वा स्वकीयजघने तयोः ॥
5.45.m: Saying 'So be it,' the Lord raised his blazing discus, / placed their heads on his own thighs, and severed them.

5.45.s:
evaṃ te kathito rājan kālikāyāḥ samudbhavaḥ |
mahālakṣmyāstathotpattiṃ niśāmaya mahāmate ||
nirvikārādi sākārā nirākārāpi devyumā |
devānāṃ tāpanāśārthaṃ prādurāsīdyuge yuge ||
5.45.d:
एवं ते कथितो राजन् कालिकायाः समुद्भवः ।
महालक्ष्म्यास्तथोत्पत्तिं निशामय महामते ॥
निर्विकारादि साकारा निराकारापि देव्युमा ।
देवानां तापनाशार्थं प्रादुरासीद्युगे युगे ॥
5.45.m:
Thus the emergence of Kālikā has been told to you, O king. / Hear now, O noble-minded one, the manifestation of Mahālakṣmī.

Though without form, changeless and the beginning of all, the goddess Umā, possessing form, / manifested age after age to dispel the distress of the gods.

5.45.s:
yadicchāvaibhavaṃ sarvaṃ tasyā dehagrahaḥ smṛtaḥ |
līlayā sāpi bhaktānāṃ guṇavarṇanahetave ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.45.d:
यदिच्छावैभवं सर्वं तस्या देहग्रहः स्मृतः ।
लीलया सापि भक्तानां गुणवर्णनहेतवे ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.45.m:
Her assumption of a body is traditionally known to be wholly the power of her will, / undertaken as sport for the sake of the devotees’ recounting her virtues.

Homage to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara!

5.46.s:
ṛṣiruvāca |
āsīdrambhāsuro nāma daityavaṃśaśiromaṇiḥ |
tasmājjāto mahātejā mahiṣo nāma dānavaḥ ||
5.46.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
आसीद्रम्भासुरो नाम दैत्यवंशशिरोमणिः ।
तस्माज्जातो महातेजा महिषो नाम दानवः ॥
5.46.m: The sage said: / There was an asura named Rambha, the crest-jewel of the daitya lineage; / from him was born a dānava of immense splendor named Mahiṣa.

5.46.s:
sa saṅgrāme surānsarvānnirjitya danujādhipaḥ |
cakāra rājyaṃ svarloke mahendrāsanasaṃsthitaḥ ||
5.46.d:
स सङ्ग्रामे सुरान्सर्वान्निर्जित्य दनुजाधिपः ।
चकार राज्यं स्वर्लोके महेन्द्रासनसंस्थितः ॥
5.46.m: Having conquered all the gods in battle, that lord of the danujas / ruled the heavenly realm, seated on the throne of Mahendra.

5.46.s:
parājitāstato devā brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ |
brahmāpi tānsamādāya yayau yatra vṛṣākapī ||
5.46.d:
पराजितास्ततो देवा ब्रह्माणं शरणं ययुः ।
ब्रह्मापि तान्समादाय ययौ यत्र वृषाकपी ॥
5.46.m: Vanquished, the gods then went to Brahmā for refuge; / Brahmā too, taking them with him, went to where Vṛṣākapī [and Śambhu] were.

5.46.s:
tatra gatvā surāḥ sarve natvā śaṅkarakeśavau |
svavṛttaṃ kathāyāmāsuryathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ ||
5.46.d:
तत्र गत्वा सुराः सर्वे नत्वा शङ्करकेशवौ ।
स्ववृत्तं कथायामासुर्यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥
5.46.m: Having gone there and bowed to Śaṅkara and Keśava, all the gods / related their situation properly and in succession:

5.46.s:
bhagavantau vayaṃ sarve mahiṣeṇa durātmanā |
ujjāsitāśca svarlokānnirjitya samarāṅgaṇe ||
5.46.d:
भगवन्तौ वयं सर्वे महिषेण दुरात्मना ।
उज्जासिताश्च स्वर्लोकान्निर्जित्य समराङ्गणे ॥
5.46.m: 'O Lords, all of us have been conquered on the battleground / and driven out of the heavenly realm by the wicked Mahiṣa.

5.46.s:
bhramāmo martyaloke'sminna labhemahiśaṃ kvacit |
kāṃ kāṃ na durdaśāṃ nītā devā indrapurogamāḥ ||
5.46.d:
भ्रमामो मर्त्यलोकेऽस्मिन्न लभेमहिशं क्वचित् ।
कां कां न दुर्दशां नीता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः ॥
5.46.m: We wander about in this mortal world and find no peace anywhere; / to what wretched state have the gods, led by Indra, not been brought?

5.46.s:
sūryācandramasau pāśī kubero yama eva ca |
indrāgnivātagandharvā vidyādharasucāraṇāḥ ||
5.46.d:
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ पाशी कुबेरो यम एव च ।
इन्द्राग्निवातगन्धर्वा विद्याधरसुचारणाः ॥
5.46.m: The Sun and the Moon, the wielder of the noose [Varuṇa], Kubera, and Yama, / Indra, Agni, Vāta, the gandharvas, vidyādharas, and good cāraṇas—

5.46.s:
eteṣāmapareṣāṃ ca vidheyaṃ karma so'suraḥ |
svayaṃ karoti pāpātmā daityapakṣābhayaṅkara ||
5.46.d:
एतेषामपरेषां च विधेयं कर्म सोऽसुरः ।
स्वयं करोति पापात्मा दैत्यपक्षाभयङ्कर ॥
5.46.m: the duties assigned to these and others, that sinful asura / performs himself, granting security to the faction of the daityas.

5.46.s:
tasmāccharaṇamāpannāndevānnastrātumarhathaḥ |
vadhopāyaṃ ca tasyāśu cintayethāṃ yuvāṃ prabhū ||
5.46.d:
तस्माच्छरणमापन्नान्देवान्नस्त्रातुमर्हथः ।
वधोपायं च तस्याशु चिन्तयेथां युवां प्रभू ॥
5.46.m: Therefore you two ought to protect us gods who have approached you for refuge, / and you two lords should promptly devise a means for his destruction.'

5.46.s:
iti devavacaḥ śrutvā dāmodarasatīśvarau |
cakratuḥ paramaṃ kopaṃ roṣāghūrṇitalocanau ||
5.46.d:
इति देववचः श्रुत्वा दामोदरसतीश्वरौ ।
चक्रतुः परमं कोपं रोषाघूर्णितलोचनौ ॥
5.46.m: Hearing this speech of the gods, Dāmodara and the Lord of Satī / were filled with extreme anger, their eyes rolling with wrath.

5.46.s:
tato'tikopapūrṇasya viṣṇoḥ śambhośca vaktrataḥ |
tathānyeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ śarīrānnirgataṃ mahaḥ ||
5.46.d:
ततोऽतिकोपपूर्णस्य विष्णोः शम्भोश्च वक्त्रतः ।
तथान्येषां च देवानां शरीरान्निर्गतं महः ॥
5.46.m: Then from the mouth of Viṣṇu, full of intense fury, and from Śambhu’s, / and likewise from the bodies of the other gods, a brilliant light emerged.

5.46.s:
atīva mahasaḥ puñjaṃ jvalantaṃ daśadikṣu ca |
apaśyaṃstridaśāḥ sarve durgādhyānaparāyaṇāḥ ||
5.46.d:
अतीव महसः पुञ्जं ज्वलन्तं दशदिक्षु च ।
अपश्यंस्त्रिदशाः सर्वे दुर्गाध्यानपरायणाः ॥
5.46.m: A tremendous mass of light blazing in the ten directions / all the gods saw, wholly intent on meditating upon Durgā.

5.46.s:
sarvadevaśarīrotthaṃ tejastadatibhīṣaṇam |
saṅghībhūyābhavannārī sākṣānmahiṣamardinī ||
5.46.d:
सर्वदेवशरीरोत्थं तेजस्तदतिभीषणम् ।
सङ्घीभूयाभवन्नारी साक्षान्महिषमर्दिनी ॥
5.46.m: Arising from the bodies of all the gods, that terrifying splendor, / coalescing, became a woman: Mahiṣamardinī manifest.

5.46.s:
śambhutejasa utpannaṃ mukhamasyāḥ subhāsvaram |
yāmyena bālā abhavanvaiṣṇavena ca bāhavaḥ ||
5.46.d:
शम्भुतेजस उत्पन्नं मुखमस्याः सुभास्वरम् ।
याम्येन बाला अभवन्वैष्णवेन च बाहवः ॥
5.46.m: Her dazzling face was produced from the splendor of Śambhu; / her hair arose from that of Yama, and her arms from that of Viṣṇu.

5.46.s:
candramastejasā tasyāḥ stanayugmaṃ vyajāyata |
madhyamaindreṇa jaṅghorū vāruṇena babhūvatuḥ ||
5.46.d:
चन्द्रमस्तेजसा तस्याः स्तनयुग्मं व्यजायत ।
मध्यमैन्द्रेण जङ्घोरू वारुणेन बभूवतुः ॥
5.46.m: From the splendor of the Moon her pair of breasts was born; / her waist came from Indra's, and her shanks and thighs from Varuṇa's.

5.46.s:
bhūtejasā nitambo'bhūd brāhmeṇa caraṇadvayam |
ārkeṇa caraṇāṅgulyaḥ karāṅgulyaśca vāsavāt ||
5.46.d:
भूतेजसा नितम्बोऽभूद् ब्राह्मेण चरणद्वयम् ।
आर्केण चरणाङ्गुल्यः कराङ्गुल्यश्च वासवात् ॥
5.46.m: Her hips arose from the splendor of the Earth, her pair of feet from Brahmā's, / her toes from the Sun's, and her fingers from Indra's.

5.46.s:
kuberatejasā nāsā radanāśca prajāpateḥ |
pāvakīyena nayanatrayaṃ sāndhyena bhrūdvayam ||
5.46.d:
